articles.title_orig: Rumor: Apple to Announce New Partnership With ADT
articles.title_zh: Rumor: Apple to Announce New Partnership With ADT
articles.content_orig:
Apple may be planning to announce a new partnership with home security company ADT, alongside the introduction of its all-new smart home hub , according to several clues. Apple has invited the media to a "Welcome home" experience in New York on Tuesday, October 13 , so the partnership could be made official on that day.
Since around July, ADT has posted "Low Voltage Technician" job listings in various U.S. cities, but those hired for the position so far have been provided with very few details about their specific responsibilities. In recent months, some of these people said they have primarily been shadowing other ADT technicians while they await further information. In addition, some of the employees and their managers said they signed a non-disclosure agreement (NDA) related to the role. This high level of secrecy is very common for Apple.
Another potential giveaway is that ADT has provided these new hires with iPhones for work, whereas its other technicians have received Android devices.
A third clue is that some of the new hires said ADT finally plans to share more details about the role later this month, so the company may be waiting for Apple to announce its smart home hub on Tuesday. Apple is also expected to unveil an ecosystem of third-party smart home accessories it developed in partnership with brands such as LG .
One of the new hires said ADT initially planned to provide details about the role in September, but later delayed this timeframe until October. This would be consistent with reports that Apple has postponed the announcement of its home hub multiple times, as Siri AI was not ready. The revamped version of Siri finally launched last month.
In addition to Siri AI, the home hub will reportedly offer smart home accessory management, home security monitoring, photo faces and galleries, an overview of calendar appointments, music playback, FaceTime video calling, and more. The hub will reportedly be available in a tabletop version with a speaker base and a wall-mounted version.
Some of the new hires who asked their managers about the secretive role were told that it will apparently relate to home automation and in-home installation services, so perhaps Apple will announce an option for customers to have an ADT technician professionally install the wall-mounted home hub or the related accessories from LG.
It is unclear if Apple's partnership with ADT would extend to home security monitoring.
ADT already reached a home security partnership with Google in 2023 , but it reportedly dropped some features that it offered on Google Nest devices earlier this year. A few people familiar with the matter told us that ADT's agreement with Google either already expired this year or will expire next year and is not set to be renewed. If this is true, then it would pave the way for ADT to reach a partnership with another tech giant: Apple.
Keep in mind that a potential partnership between Apple and ADT is still just a rumor for now, and all of these clues could somehow prove to be one big coincidence. But if the partnership does become official on Tuesday, you heard it here first.

articles.title_orig: Shooter kills 8 people and himself in Pennsylvania, police say, with Governor Shapiro offering support
articles.title_zh: Shooter kills 8 people and himself in Pennsylvania, police say, with Governor Shapiro offering support
articles.content_orig:
A man killed eight people and himself during a mass shooting at a house in Erie, Pennsylvania, local police said Saturday.
Erie Police Chief Rick Lorah said seven of the eight victims were related to the shooter, with the eighth person being a family friend. The shooter had died of an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound before authorities arrived at the scene.
Among the victims was a 1-year-old girl and 5-year-old boy, with a pregnant woman also dead in the shooting.
"Some scenes stay with you long after you leave them. This is one of those tragic scenes," Lorah said, describing an "eerie silence" when police arrived at the home.
The identity of the 45-year-old shooter has not yet been revealed by authorities. The motive for the massacre is also still unclear, with police pursuing an investigation .
At a press conference, Erie Mayor Daria Devlin addressed the families of the victims.
"I am so deeply sorry. What happened to you was horrific, and there is nothing that any of us can say today that will make this any easier," she said. "But you do need to know that our entire community is with you, we're grieving with you. And we are here to support you."
Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro spoke with Devlin by phone and offered his support to Erie.
"I've spoken with Mayor Devlin and offered my administration's full support following the tragic mass shooting in Erie last night — killing nine of our fellow Pennsylvanians," Shapiro said in a statement post on X.
Shapiro said his "heart breaks for this family" and added that he and his wife Lori Shapiro "are praying for their loved ones and the entire Erie community."
Shapiro, a Democrat , has pushed for gun control bills in his state and signed an executive order in 2024 to reestablish the Pennsylvania Office of Gun Violence Prevention.

articles.title_orig: Alabama vs. Georgia live updates: No. 6 Crimson Tide meet No. 2 Bulldogs in pivotal SEC showdown
articles.title_zh: Alabama vs. Georgia live updates: No. 6 Crimson Tide meet No. 2 Bulldogs in pivotal SEC showdown
articles.content_orig:
Two of the SEC's three remaining undefeated teams will battle it out Saturday night inside Bryant-Denny Stadium.
No. 2 Georgia is a 2.5-point underdog on the road at No. 6 Alabama (7:30 p.m. ET on ABC). All week attention centered on the potential impact of Hurricane Isaias on the night game between the two SEC heavyweights. While central Alabama received plenty of rain overnight and through the afternoon, Isaias devolved into a post-tropical system by Saturday morning. The weather will likely have a more limited impact than was initially feared earlier in the week.
What we should see Saturday night is one of the most explosive offenses in the country versus one of the best defenses especially when it comes to stopping the run. Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell has been terrific this season for the Crimson Tide, throwing for 1,1414 yards, 14 touchdowns and only two interceptions. His favorite target has been Ryan Coleman-Williams who leads the team with 376 receiving yards and four touchdowns.
Georgia has dominated all the competition it has faced this season but gets its toughest test yet against Alabama. He doesn't get as much attention as Russell, but Georgia quarterback Gunner Stockton has been very good for the Bulldogs. He has 13 touchdowns to only one interception and has ably guided the UGA offense to big wins over opponents like Oklahoma and Vanderbilt. The Bulldogs are expected to have leading rusher Nate Frazier closer to full strength after missing most of the last two games.
Not only would the winner of this game be in prime early position to make the SEC Championship but would have a better than 93 percent chance to make the College Football Playoff, according to CBS Sports' forecasting and projections team.
Keep it locked here as CBS Sports provides you with live updates, highlights and analysis as Alabama battles Georgia on Saturday.
A tipped INT notwithstanding, Gunner Stockton is having himself a helluva game in Tuscaloosa. He's made multiple big-time throws tonight including a 30-yard one to Craig Dandridge that was right on the money in tight coverage. Stockton then kept it to himself and scored on a 14-yard run.
He's 11 for 13 for 188 yards, one passing touchdown, one rushing touchdown and an interception. That was a strong response from Georgia to start the second half after the way Alabama took the lead right before the half.
A gutsy decision from Kalen DeBoer right before halftime paid off as EJ Crowell raced in from a yard out to give No. 6 Alabama a 14-10 lead over No. 2 Georgia. The Bulldogs will start with the ball in the second half.
Facing a second-and-goal from Georgia's 1-yard line with only time for one more play, DeBoer opted to run the ball with Crowell, who was able to get the edge on a Georgia defender and run in for the touchdown. It was an impressive two-minute drive from Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell and the Crimson Tide offense after the defense stopped Georgia.
Georgia struck first off a 42-yard Peyton Woodring field goal in the first quarter for a 3-0 lead. The Bulldogs added to that with a Gunner Stockton to London Humphreys 20-yard touchdown pass. Stockton was efficient and effective in the first half, finishing 9 for 11 for 143 yards, one touchdown and an interception. Stockton set up the touchdown drive with a 53-yard pass to Jaden Reddell, who raced down the middle of the field.
Alabama wasn't able to muster as many explosive plays as fans have become accustomed to seeing this season, but finally broke through in the second quarter. Trae'shawn Brown gave Alabama the big play it desperately needed with a 58-yard run. One play later, Keelon Russell got Alabama on the board with a 22-yard touchdown pass to Marshall Pritchett. Russell didn't look particularly comfortable early on against the Bulldogs, but settled in nicely in the second quarter. He finished the half 11 for 22 for 119 yards, one touchdown and one lost fumble.
Alabama outgained Georgia, 224-192, in the first half.
Alabama's defense is facing a critical series here coming out of the two-minute timeout. Georgia is on its own 42-yard line with all three timeouts remaining and set up to get the ball to start the second half. Gunner Stockton has been moving the ball well. Georgia adding another touchdown right before halftime could be a backbreaker.
Alabama has had some success bringing extra pressure on Stockton. Can it dial it up a bit more to force a punt?
No team had more explosive plays than Alabama coming into tonight's game. Through the first quarter-and-a-half, though, Alabama couldn't manage much. And then came the big breakthrough on a Trae'shawn Brown 58-yard run. The very next play Keelon Russell connected with Marshall Pritchett for a 22-yard touchdown.
Georgia jumping out to a 10-0 lead quieted the crowd but two big plays back-to-back after the place roaring again.
Gunner Stockton threw a dart to Jaden Reddell who raced past a step-too-slow Bray Hubbard down the middle of the field for a 53-yard gain. The very next play Stockton hit London Humphreys for a 20-yard touchdown to give Georgia a two-score lead and completely quieted the Bryant-Denny Stadium crowd. Alabama had been doing a good job bottling up Georgia's offense before Stockton found something he liked down the middle.
Stockton is a perfect 6 for 6 for 109 yards and a touchdown.
It has turned into a defensive slugfest here in the first half. Georgia is all over Keelon Russell, who hasn't looked super comfortable early on in this one. He's 4 for 7 for 24 yards and a lost fumble. The big play opportunities Russell excelled at last week against Mississippi State haven't been there.
Similarly, Alabama's defense hasn't given Georgia much to work with. After a terrific Alabama punt was downed at Georgia's 3-yard line, the Bulldogs couldn't manage much and had to punt after a three-and-out. Gunner Stockton is 2 for 2 for 29 yards.
Despite the penalties, Georgia put three points on the board off a Peyton Woodring 43-yard field goal. Dwight Phillips had 16 rushing yards -- plus a 17-yard rushing touchdown that was called back -- while Gunner Stockton connected with Lawson Luckie for a 26-yard gain to power Georgia's early offense.
Georgia appeared to have the first points of the game on a Dwight Phillips touchdown run...until a holding penalty brought it back. It wasn't an egregious hold but was just enough right in front of an official to get called. On the next play, Georgia got hit for a rare offensive pass interference call on a pick play that resulted in an injury to Jaden Reddell.
If Georgia doesn't emerge with points from this drive, those penalties will loom extra large.
A promising first drive for Alabama ends when Keelon Russell gets hit from his blind side and fumbles the ball on Georgia's 37-yard line. Russell didn't have much of a shot with Joseph Jonah-Ajonye on him as quickly as he was. The Bulldogs get the ball on their 39-yard line.
We are just about to kick off here in Bryant-Denny Stadium. Georgia won the toss and has chosen to defer. It's been a rainy day in Alabama, and we'll see how it impacts Keelon Russell and this high-powered Alabama offense to start.
For all the incredible success Kirby Smart has had at Georgia, Alabama has remained a quandary he rarely has been able to figure out. Smart has a 122-21 record while at UGA, and yet seven of those 21 losses have come at the hands of the Crimson Tide. Smart beat Alabama in last season's SEC Championship -- his first win in four tries against Bama in Atlanta -- but has yet to win a regular-season game. Smart is 0-3 all-time against Alabama, with the last two coming in back-to-back seasons against Kalen DeBoer.
Can Kirby get his first regular-season win over Alabama tonight? His Bulldogs are 2.5-point underdogs on the road.

articles.title_orig: Roman Reigns slams the door on LA Knight’s world title hopes after incredible match at Money in the Bank | OutKick
articles.title_zh: Roman Reigns slams the door on LA Knight’s world title hopes after incredible match at Money in the Bank | OutKick
articles.content_orig:
It was now or never for LA Knight in his pursuit of a world title. On Saturday night at Money in the Bank, Roman Reigns made sure it was never.
Reigns slammed the door shut on Knight’s World Heavyweight Championship hopes, successfully defending the title at the Smoothie King Center in New Orleans in front of a hot crowd that was on the edge of their seat throughout the entire match.

Sure, fans appeared to be in Reigns’ corner. They acknowledged him. They chanted "OTC." But as Knight came with in a millisecond of pinning Reigns, the crowd turned. They wanted to see Knight pull off the impossible in what was the best match of his WWE career up to this point.
Knight pulled out all the stops. He nailed a jumping superplex and put Reins into the Burning Hammer. He couldn’t get the pain. He ate multiple Superman punches and kept his shoulders off the mat. He avoided a spear and countered with a BFT. Outside of the ring, Knight avoided Reigns’ attempt to spear him through the barricade. Then, he powerbombed him through the announce table.
The challenger brought Reigns back into the ring and still couldn’t get the win. The yelps were loud in my house as Knight nearly got the pinfall multiple times.

articles.title_orig: 26% in Japan see U.S. as biggest threat to world peace: survey
articles.title_zh: 26% in Japan see U.S. as biggest threat to world peace: survey
articles.content_orig:
A media association survey has found that the proportion of people in Japan who think the United States is the biggest threat to world peace came to 26.8%, the second highest after China, cited by 32.5%.
The rate for the United States rose 9.3 percentage points from the previous fiscal 2025 survey. The figure stood at 6.6% in fiscal 2024.
In the Japan Press Research Institute’s latest survey, released Saturday, participants were asked to pick one of the eight choices, including Russia and North Korea, as the country that they think poses the greatest threat to world peace.
China was up from second place, with its share rising 8.2 points.
Selected by 18.3%, Russia fell to third after ranking top in preceding surveys.
North Korea remained fourth, with 9.1%, while Iran, which has been in a military conflict with the United States, was chosen by 1.9%.
An official of the institute said that “the recognition that the United States poses a threat to the world is gradually expanding” due to the unpredictability of actions by U.S. President Donald Trump.
In the survey, a total of 82.5% of respondents said that Trump is having a negative impact on the world, including those who somewhat think so, up 3.1 points. The share of respondents who think Trump is having a positive impact came to 13.2%.
The survey also showed that 76.7% “very much” have or “somewhat” have a sense of crisis about a potential Taiwan contingency.
The survey was conducted between July 17 and Aug. 16, covering 5,000 people age 18 or over across Japan. Valid responses were received from 2,676.

A federal judge in California has sentenced a former Syrian prison warden to 60 years for torturing inmates and lying to immigration officials to get into the United States.
A jury convicted Samir Ousman Alsheikh, 74, in March of conspiracy to commit torture, three counts of torture, one count of visa fraud and one count of attempted naturalization fraud, according to the U.S. attorney’s office in Los Angeles.
Alsheikh was involved in torturing political dissidents to deter opposition to the regime of then-Syrian President Bashar Assad, according to the Justice Department.
Government officials say Alsheikh is the highest-ranking former member of the Assad regime to be tried and convicted in person outside Syria.
The Justice Department had sought no fewer than 80 years in prison, while Alsheikh requested five years, citing his age and his chronic medical conditions.
In handing down the sentence on Thursday, U.S. District Judge Hernán Vera remarked on the “utter reprehensibility” of Alsheikh’s crime, Courthouse News Service reported .
“The conduct was heinous, unimaginably cruel and unspeakably violent and brutal,” the judge reportedly said.
Nina Marino, Alsheikh’s attorney, said her client plans to appeal the sentence.
In a statement, First Assistant U.S. Atty. Bill Essayli said he hoped the sentence “gives some semblance of healing and closure to this defendant’s victims.”
“Criminals who inflict the type of savage brutality that this defendant did on his victims must never be granted refuge in our country,” Essayli said.
Samir Ousman Sheikh allegedly ordered inmates to a wing of a Syrian prison where they were then tortured with a device known as the ‘flying carpet.’
During Alsheikh’s trial, prosecutors presented evidence that Alsheikh ordered and participated in the torture of prisoners while he headed the Adra Prison, also known as Damascus Central Prison, from around 2005 to 2008.
Jurors heard testimony from three of Alsheikh’s victims who said they were packed into small, filthy, cold, wet cells that were infested with insects and other vermin. They described being tortured and seeing and hearing the torture of other prisoners.
The victims testified about being fastened to a device known as the “Flying Carpet,” which folded their bodies in half at the waist; about being manacled to the ceiling and suspended sometimes for days; and about being beaten while immobilized inside tires, according to the U.S. attorney’s office in L.A.
During the trial, prosecutors presented evidence that when detainees refused Alsheikh’s orders to harm political prisoners, he ordered them to be sent to an underground section of the prison known as Wing 13, where they were tortured.
Prosecutors also presented evidence that Alsheikh, who came to the country in 2020, lied to U.S. immigration authorities about his background to secure a green card and also on an application to naturalize as a U.S. citizen.
Alsheikh has been in custody since his arrest at Los Angeles International Airport in July 2024.
Khaled Abdul Malek, who testified about being detained and tortured under Alsheikh’s direction, praised the sentence in a statement .
“The land of freedom will never be a safe haven for slaughterers and those who committed crimes against humanity,” Malek said. “This trial is not the end, but the first step on the road toward accountability and justice for everyone whose hands have been stained with the blood of innocent people.”

President Trump spoke with Russian leader Vladimir Putin on Friday to discuss freeing up millions of tons of diesel , but the Russian president also relayed Iran's position on a peace deal to his American counterpart, according to the Kremlin.
The U.S. military disabled a Panama-flagged commercial vessel in the Gulf of Oman Saturday by firing on it with a fighter jet, U.S. military's Central Command said.
According to CENTCOM, the fighter jet fired a "precision munition" at M/V Ocean Molica, also known as the "Arika Sun," that disabled the "ship's propulsion without harming the crew."
The ship had recently departed an Iranian port. Iran's ports have been under a U.S. blockade since a ceasefire between the two countries collapsed in July.
Four commercial vessels have been disabled by U.S. forces and 135 ships have been turned around since the blockade took effect on July 14, CENTCOM said.
During that same period, U.S. forces have also destroyed 10 tankers that are believed to be part of a "shadow fleet" that transport sanctioned Iranian oil and petroleum products, CENTCOM said.
At least 12 people were killed and 309 others wounded in a strike Saturday on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport, Saudi officials said.
In a statement , the Saudi General Authority of Civil Aviation said an American was among the 12 victims. Four Saudi nationals, two Bangladeshi nationals, one Egyptian, one Jordanian, one Syrian, one Palestinian and one Sudanese national were also among those killed.
Another 309 people were wounded, the civil aviation authority said, an unknown number of whom were in critical condition.
The U.S. State Department has blamed the Iran-backed Houthi militant group for the strike, although the Houthis have not claimed responsibility for it.
"The United States strongly condemns the recent attacks on the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia by the terrorist Houthis, including today's strike on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh that took numerous innocent lives, including an American citizen," Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in a social media post.
A violent conflict between a Saudi-backed coalition that supports the Yemeni government and the Houthis, who control a large swath of Yemen, has been building for weeks as the Houthis have expanded control of Yemen's Red Sea coastline and several islands in the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a critical waterway that has put further pressure on the movement of oil globally.
Earlier Saturday, President Trump said he was considering whether to have the U.S. join the fight against the Houthis.
The Saudi-led international coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis said Saturday a "projectile" fell near Dammam's international airport, hours after officials acknowledged an attack on Riyadh's airport.
"A projectile landed near King Fahd International Airport in Dammam," wrote the coalition spokesman on X.
The U.S. State Department on Saturday condemned what it called "Houthi terrorist attacks against civilian infrastructure and airports" in Saudi Arabia.
A State Department spokesperson told CBS News it is in close contact with its "Saudi partners."
The Houthis have not claimed responsibility for Saturday's strike on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport, in which there were multiple injuries and fatalities, according to the State Department. The airport's operations have been shut down, according to Saudi Arabia's aviation authority.
" The United States stands firmly with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia against Houthi terrorism," the spokesperson said.
President Trump left open the possibility the U.S. will join Saudi Arabia's battle against the Iran-backed Houthis on Saturday.
"We may. We're gonna look at it," Mr. Trump said when asked about the possibility as he left the White House for a campaign rally in Tennessee. "We just found out about the recent attack [on the airport]. So we'll make a decision– we move very quickly."
Mr. Trump was also asked about whether the Houthi strike on Riyadh's airport would change his previously announced decision not to launch any potential strikes on Iran until after the midterms.
"Well, we're gonna take a look," he responded.
Multiple people were injured in a strike on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport on Saturday. The Houthis have not claimed responsibility for the attack, but Saudi Arabia's aviation authority said the strike was part of "continued attacks targeting civil aviation facilities in the Kingdom."
There have been multiple injuries at Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport, which has now shut down operations as officials assess the damage, according to the country's aviation authority.
"The attack resulted in a number of injuries, which are being dealt with," the General Authority of Civil Aviation said in a statement, the first official confirmation of an attack. "The authority explained that airport operations have been temporarily suspended to allow for the completion of damage assessments and verification of the safety of the facilities, in coordination with the relevant authorities."
There have been 324 flights into or out of King Khalid International Airport canceled on Saturday, according to FlightAware. Saudia airline, a pilot for which was killed in a Houthi strike on Thursday, has canceled the most flights (182) on Saturday.
The Iran-backed Houthis have gotten more bold in striking the airport, which is a major travel hub and hundreds of miles from where their power is located in Yemen. The militant organization has targeted the Riyadh airport several times this week, killing four people and injuring several more. Multiple people were also injured in a strike on Abha International Airport, in the southern part of Saudi Arabia.
The U.S. is warning all citizens to avoid King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh in the wake of new attacks on the location Saturday, the embassy said.
"The U.S. Mission is aware of attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on October 10 and strongly recommends all U.S. citizens avoid this airport and surrounding areas," the U.S. Embassy in Saudi Arabia said on X . "U.S. government employees working in Saudi Arabia require special authorization to use the King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh. U.S. citizens should be aware of potential flight cancellations, airspace closures, and travel disruptions."
While the airport nor the Iran-backed Houthis have confirmed an attack, there were widespread reports of an explosion at the main airport in Saudi's capital and reports of injuries.
The Houthis have attacked the airport, which is hundreds of miles north of the Yemen border, several times this week. Four people have been killed in Houthi attacks on the airport, including three people on Thursday. One of those killed was a pilot for Saudia airline.
The Canadian, German and Spanish embassies in Saudi Arabia on Saturday warned their citizens to avoid Riyadh's international airport after reports it was attacked.
Spain's embassy, in a message on X, alerted nationals to a "new attack" by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis on the airport, where witnesses earlier told AFP an evacuation was ordered.
A diplomatic source separately told AFP that the Houthis had hit the airport with a missile around 3 p.m. local time.
Canada's embassy said only that unspecified "ongoing military activity" was affecting Riyadh's international airport, while Germany's mission alluded only to "the current situation."
France's embassy on Friday urged French nationals to take "utmost care" in Saudi Arabia because of "strikes in recent days by the Houthis." It also warned French citizens not to record images of zones that were hit, nor share any online.
Saudi Arabia has been tightly controlling public information about Houthi attacks on its soil in recent weeks, leaving media and residents unclear as to the danger.

articles.title_orig: China Expands Its Presence In Peru’s Critical Electricity Infrastructure – Analysis
articles.title_zh: China Expands Its Presence In Peru’s Critical Electricity Infrastructure – Analysis
articles.content_orig:
The Chaglla hydroelectric plant in Huánuco, Peru, is part of China Three Gorges Corporation’s growing presence in the Peruvian electricity sector. The 456 MW plant is operated by Empresa de Generación Huallaga, which is affiliated with the Chinese group. (Photo: Peru’s Ministry of Energy and Mines)
State-owned China Three Gorges Corporation (CTG) expanded its presence in Peru’s electricity sector in 2026 by acquiring the remaining stake in Hydro Global Perú, a company linked to the San Gabán III hydroelectric plant in Puno. The transaction adds to the group’s other major assets in the country, including the Chaglla hydroelectric plant in the department of Huánuco and Luz del Sur, one of Peru’s leading electricity distributors.
CTG’s expansion has unfolded over several years. In 2019, the company completed its acquisition of Chaglla, a 456-megawatt (MW) facility and Peru’s third-largest hydroelectric plant. Chinese state-owned companies subsequently expanded their presence into other segments of Peru’s electricity market, including power distribution in Lima and Callao.
“In recent years, South American governments have shown great interest in developing international partnerships to better develop their energy resources and improve the reliability of their power grids,” Peruvian analyst Pedro Yaranga told Diálogo . “China took advantage of that opening to become the leading investor and lender in Latin America and the Caribbean’s energy sector.”
More than 80 power generation companies, 21 transmission companies, and 23 distribution companies operate in Peru. The two largest distributors are Pluz Energía, controlled by China Southern Power Grid International , and Luz del Sur, owned by China Three Gorges Corporation. Together, they serve nearly 3 million customers and account for one-third of the national electricity distribution market, according to Dialogue Earth .
Yaranga distinguishes between two areas of that presence. “Chinese investments in South American energy infrastructure span two distinct sectors: generation and distribution,” he said. Generation produces electricity at hydroelectric, thermal, wind, or solar facilities; transmission carries electricity at high voltage across the power system, while distribution ultimately delivers it to homes, businesses, and public facilities.
China’s footprint extends beyond the electricity sector. Writing in the Argentine newspaper La Nación , international relations specialist Patricio Carmody said China has invested in Peru’s mining — including copper and iron — infrastructure, and energy sectors. According to Carmody, Chinese investments total $30 billion, equivalent to 25 percent of foreign direct investment. The deep-water Port of Chancay , operated by Chinese company COSCO, provides a direct maritime route to Shanghai and also aims to establish itself as an export gateway for Brazil. Combined with the presence of Chinese state-owned companies in electricity distribution in Lima and Callao, these investments have raised concerns about growing dependence, Carmody said.
That expansion could continue. Peru’s Ministry of Energy and Mines estimates the country’s hydroelectric potential at approximately 70,000 MW, its largest renewable energy resource alongside wind, geothermal, and solar resources. About 8 percent of that potential is currently being harnessed, while projects under development represent another 4 percent.
Peru is not alone. In Chile, state-owned State Grid Corporation of China controls Compañía General de Electricidad (CGE) and Chilquinta Energía, two of the country’s leading electricity distributors. Through those acquisitions, the company accounts for approximately 57 percent of customers in Chile’s electricity distribution market . In Brazil, State Grid Corporation of China has also expanded its presence in transmission infrastructure, including an extensive direct-current transmission line designed to carry renewable energy from the northeast to the country’s main consumption centers.
In Ecuador, the Coca Codo Sinclair hydroelectric plant, built by Chinese company Sinohydro, a subsidiary of state-owned PowerChina , has faced years of technical problems and controversies related to its construction. In August 2026, an Ecuadorian court convicted 20 people of bribery in a scheme involving illicit payments tied to the awarding and execution of the project.
China’s economic expansion also comes with a central diplomatic condition from Beijing: Countries that establish official relations with the People’s Republic of China must end diplomatic recognition of Taiwan. Honduras established diplomatic relations with Beijing in March 2023, while Nicaragua did so in December 2021. Chinese companies have subsequently participated in infrastructure and energy projects in both countries, including hydroelectric and solar projects.
The scale of these investments is redefining Beijing’s role in the hemisphere. “China is no longer merely a buyer of raw materials; it is becoming deeply embedded in key sectors across the region, including lithium, copper, ports, telecommunications, artificial intelligence, mining, energy, digital surveillance, and electric mobility,” Yaranga said.
In early September, Chinese Ambassador to Peru Song Yang met with business leaders in the Pacific coastal department of La Libertad and representatives of Chinese companies to explore new opportunities in energy, technology, trade, infrastructure, and logistics. During the meeting, Pluz Energía representatives highlighted the need to expand electricity infrastructure to support industrialization and proposed electrifying freight transportation to the Port of Chancay. COSCO Shipping representatives also explored logistics and commercial opportunities with companies in the region.
The growing presence of Chinese companies in strategic sectors raises challenges that go beyond commercial competition. Those concerns are not limited to state-owned companies: China’s legal framework also requires private companies and other organizations to cooperate with authorities on national security and intelligence matters. That relationship takes on particular significance in sectors such as energy, where operations depend on digital systems, communications, and data .
In Peru, the Supervisory Agency for Investment in Energy and Mining (Osinergmin) and the National Institute for the Defense of Competition and Protection of Intellectual Property (Indecopi) retain regulatory oversight of the sector. “It is essential to remain vigilant about the control Chinese companies exercise over critical infrastructure, such as electricity distribution, which could compromise energy sovereignty,” Yaranga said. He called for robust laws to protect strategic assets and prevent monopolies imposed by Beijing.
With only 8 percent of Peru’s hydroelectric potential currently being harnessed, considerable room remains for new investment. Strengthening oversight, diversifying sources of investment, and preventing greater dependence on Chinese companies will be key to preserving Peruvian control over infrastructure essential to the country’s security and development.

articles.title_orig: ‘Not Pleasant’ but ‘Necessary’: Support at Trump Rally for Public Execution
articles.title_zh: ‘Not Pleasant’ but ‘Necessary’: Support at Trump Rally for Public Execution
articles.content_orig:
The man who fatally shot 13 people at Fort Hood in 2009 is set to be executed, and the nature of his planned execution is quite unusual. President Trump has authorized the convicted murderer to be killed by firing squad, and now the Pentagon says the execution will be livestreamed after Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth said it would be public, an announcement that has drawn horror and condemnation.
The Trump administration's plans to carry out the death sentence against Fort Hood mass shooter Nidal Hasan are growing increasingly extreme. President Trump recently announced that Hasan, a former Army major who worked as a military psychiatrist prior to conducting the 2009 mass shooting, would be executed by firing squad , which would be the first military execution by firing squad since World War II. Trump recently told a cheering campaign crowd in Texas, "We recently announced that we are going to deliver FINAL justice to an evil killer, the Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan." Trump also tried to blame President Obama for not stopping the attack before telling the crowd that Hasan is "getting the death penalty by firing squad."
Now, Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth has announced that Hasan's execution will be public, and the Pentagon has since confirmed that it will be livestreamed. Appearing on the right-wing Real America's Voice streaming channel, Hegseth said the decision of executing Hasan by firing squad was a "no brainer." He also justified the decision, saying, "we'll make sure that people are able to watch it, that it's public, because people need to understand that there's serious consequences for these types of things." Hegseth and the host then reiterated the date of the execution in the style of announcers reminding viewers of an upcoming sporting event. "We'll see him on December 3," Hegseth said, with the host following up, "December 3, Fort Hood." If the execution goes forward, it would be the first public execution in the U.S. in nearly a century and the first ever to be livestreamed, NPR reported. Trump has since backed the plan. Asked about the livestream by reporters Friday, he said, "Absolutely, I approved," according to C-SPAN .
Reaction to these announcements has been intense, with many condemning the spectacle that the Trump administration is making out of the execution. Global outrage has come from a number of sources, with the United Nations human rights office saying that broadcasting an execution would "breach the absolute prohibition of torture" and British Equalities Minister Bridget Phillipson, who is also the chair of the Labour Party, calling the idea "rather disturbing." A number of voices within the United States have also objected. Rep. Suhas Subramanyam (D-Virginia) posted a list of countries that carry out public executions, including Iran, North Korea, Afghanistan, ISIS and other terrorist groups. "This is un-American. Call it off."
"There is no doubt [Hasan] deserves to die. His crimes were demonic and unforgivable—death by firing squad is borderline too merciful," posted Joe Kent, former director of the National Counterterrorism Center. "But broadcasting his execution is beneath the dignity & decency of our nation."
Independent journalist Terry Moran opined, "A government-produced death spectacle debases us as a nation." He also warned that public execution "becomes a martyrdom spectacle for terrorists."
The upcoming execution of Hasan comes as the United States debates the death penalty, an issue that has been brought back to public consciousness by the botched execution of Christa Pike . It also fuels discussion of the politics and justice of the death penalty at the federal level. Shortly before leaving office, President Biden commuted the sentences of federal prisoners on death row to life without the possibility of parole, with the exceptions of Emmanuel AME Church shooter Dylann Roof, Boston Marathon bomber Dzhokhar Tsarnaev and Tree of Life Synagogue shooter Robert Bowers. Hasan, meanwhile, is one of only four people currently on military death row .
It is unclear if Hasan will attempt to file an appeal to his coming execution date or the manner in which he is set to die. But whether or not he tries to stop or delay his sentence, the unusual method and unprecedented broadcasting decision for Hasan's execution have set off a firestorm of controversy.

articles.title_orig: What to Know About Isaias, the First Atlantic Hurricane of the Season
articles.title_zh: What to Know About Isaias, the First Atlantic Hurricane of the Season
articles.content_orig:
Live updates: Deadly post-tropical Isaias charges inland, unleashing vicious impacts on the South
Coverage for this event has ended.
As the remnants of Hurricane Isaias move farther inland Sunday, millions of people across the Northeast and Mid-Atlantic are bracing for a soggy end to the weekend, with heavy rain, flooding and even severe thunderstorms possible.
Major cities along the Interstate 95 corridor, including Washington, D.C., Baltimore, Philadelphia and New York City, could see a complete washout Sunday, with rain expected to fall throughout much of the day. Similar conditions are expected farther inland in Pittsburgh, Cleveland and Charleston, West Virginia.
Read continuous coverage from FOX Weather on the aftermath of Isaias and the storm's next chapter today here.
Hurricane Isaias left a deadly trail of destruction across the Gulf Coast after making landfall near Destin, Florida, as a Category 2 hurricane with 105-mph winds.
At least four people have died — two in Florida and two in Alabama — as powerful winds toppled trees, damaged homes and knocked out power across the region.
An apartment complex had its roof was blown off when Hurricane Isaias passed through Milton, Florida.
Nearly 900,000 customers across Florida, Alabama and Georgia initially lost power.
More than 400,000 customers remained without electricity Saturday evening as utility crews assessed damage and began restoration efforts.
A man stands beside a tree branch that crashed through the roof of his mother's home in Milton, Florida. Credit: Getty Images.
Isaias has since weakened to a post-tropical cyclone, but the storm’s impacts aren't over just yet.
The Weather Prediction Center said heavy rain and flash flooding will continue spreading across the Southeast and Southern Appalachians before the remnants move into the Mid-Atlantic and Northeast on Sunday.
Flood watches remain in effect for parts of the Southeast and Mid-Atlantic, where saturated ground, rising waterways and additional rainfall could create dangerous travel conditions into Monday.
Hurricane Isaias was no ordinary hurricane when it slammed into Florida's Gulf Coast, with some of the worst wind damage occurring in an unexpected location.
According to the FOX Forecast Center, the strongest winds and most significant damage were concentrated west of the storm's center, rather than on the eastern side, where a hurricane's most powerful winds are typically found.
So, what caused this unusual pattern?
Top wind reports during Hurricane Isaias.
The FOX Forecast Center believes Isaias was already transitioning into a non-tropical storm as it made landfall, potentially allowing a weather phenomenon known as a "sting jet" to develop.
A sting jet is a narrow band of extremely powerful winds that rushes down from higher in the atmosphere toward the ground, potentially causing intense damage in a relatively small area.
Satellite radar imagery from NOAA captured a narrow band of powerful winds near Pensacola, Florida, supporting the FOX Forecast Center's theory that a sting jet may have contributed to the unusually severe damage.
The findings suggest Isaias was undergoing significant changes as it made landfall, potentially explaining why some of its most destructive winds struck areas that typically would not experience the worst of a hurricane.
Post-tropical Cyclone Isaias is moving toward Tennessee late Saturday night, but the storm’s flood threat remains far from over across the Southeast and Southern Appalachians.
The Weather Prediction Center said Isaias was located about 75 miles south of Nashville at 10 p.m. CDT, moving northeast at 16 mph with maximum sustained winds of 25 mph and higher gusts.
11 p.m. ET Advisory from the Weather Prediction Center.
Flood watches remain in effect across portions of the Southeast and Southern Appalachians, while a high wind warning covers parts of the Southern Appalachians.
Wind advisories are also posted across portions of the Southeast and Southern Appalachians.
The storm is expected to continue moving northeast on Sunday with little change in strength during the next 24 to 36 hours before being absorbed by another area of low pressure to its east.
The WPC said the greatest threat is additional heavy rain and dangerous flooding.
The Southern Appalachians, from the western Carolinas into western Virginia, could receive another 2–5 inches of rain, with isolated totals reaching 10 inches.
Additional rainfall of 1–2 inches is possible across the Florida Big Bend and northwest Florida, pushing storm totals toward 12 inches.
FOX Forecast Center rain forecast through Sunday.
Coastal areas of the Carolinas could see another 2–4 inches, with isolated totals up to 6 inches.
The heavy rain could trigger flash, urban and river flooding, while considerable impacts — including landslides — remain possible across the Southern Appalachians.
Significant river flooding in the western Florida Panhandle is expected to crest through Sunday.
Even as Isaias loses its tropical characteristics, its moisture and broad circulation continue to fuel dangerous flooding across parts of the Southeast.
The tornado threat from Isaias isn't over yet, with another round of severe weather possible Sunday as the storm's remnants move across the East Coast.
According to the FOX Forecast Center, a Level 2 out of 5 severe weather threat stretches from Washington, D.C., to Wilmington, North Carolina, where warm, moisture-rich air could fuel strong thunderstorms.
Tornado outlook along the East Coast on Sunday.
The main concerns will be brief tornadoes that develop quickly and damaging wind gusts up to 60 mph, posing additional dangers to communities already dealing with impacts from Isaias.
The severe weather threat comes as widespread rain spreads into the Northeast and Mid-Atlantic, with conditions expected to improve Monday as the system moves offshore.
Millions across the Northeast and Mid-Atlantic are bracing for a Sunday washout as the remnants of Hurricane Isaias bring widespread rain, flooding concerns and severe thunderstorms.
According to the FOX Forecast Center, Washington, D.C., Baltimore, Philadelphia and New York City could see rain nearly all day, with widespread totals of 1 to 2 inches and locally higher amounts possible.
A Level 1 out of 4 flash flood risk stretches from New York City to Washington, D.C., south toward the Outer Banks and west into West Virginia.
Farther south, a Level 2 out of 5 severe weather threat extends from Washington to Wilmington, North Carolina, where isolated tornadoes and damaging wind gusts up to 60 mph are possible.
Conditions are expected to improve Monday as the remnants of Isaias move offshore, with lingering showers clearing by midday.
Search and rescue teams are navigating dangerous conditions in Florida's Panhandle as recovery efforts continue following Hurricane Isaias.
Palm Beach County Fire Rescue's Urban Search and Rescue Team is conducting searches across large areas of Walton County, near the Alabama border, where some roads have been washed away by the storm.
Rescue specialists are using GPS systems to relay critical information to command centers while navigating debris and downed trees. The team is equipped to clear obstacles and continue searching areas impacted by the hurricane.
Officials said Saturday marked the team's first day of search operations in the storm's aftermath.
Scattered debris covers Pensacola Beach, Florida, as the community begins cleaning up after Hurricane Isaias battered the Gulf Coast.
Florida Power & Light, the Sunshine State's largest electric utility, has restored power to more than 98,000 customers across the Florida Panhandle after tropical-storm-force winds moved out of the state early Sunday, the company said in a press release.
FPL is targeting the end of Monday to restore power to 95% of customers impacted by Hurricane Isaias, though many customers could see service return sooner.

articles.title_orig: Four dead as Isaias weakens to post-tropical cyclone after striking Florida panhandle
articles.title_zh: Four dead as Isaias weakens to post-tropical cyclone after striking Florida panhandle
articles.content_orig:
Some of deaths came from falling trees as half a million people without power and rain and flooding still a concern
At least four people were reported dead on Saturday amid Isaias after it made landfall late on Friday on Florida’s panhandle as a category 2 hurricane, according to authorities.
The storm also took down trees, knocked out electricity for hundreds of thousands and flooded highways – but as Saturday evening approached, the region was reopening.
Despite warnings of storm surges ahead of the storm, several major routes along the coast were open by daybreak on Saturday and free of downed trees and power lines typically seen after major hurricanes.
Two of the deaths reported during Isaias occurred in Escambia county, Florida , and two others were reported in Alabama , as the storm moved inland, local officials said. Of those deaths, one each occurred in Escambia and Birmingham, Alabama, when trees fell on homes.
Another person whose death was linked to Isaias was found in a closed garage with a running generator in Escambia county. Four members of that person’s family have been transported to the hospital with carbon monoxide poisoning, the Escambia sheriff’s office said.
“Don’t run any generators inside your home, it can be very, very hazardous,” Florida governor Ron DeSantis said in a press conference.
In Alabama , governor Kay Ivey said Isaias – predicted to dissipate on Sunday – “cannot clear fast enough”.
Meanwhile, though it had weakened on Saturday to a post-tropical cyclone as it passed through central Alabama, Isaias still posed flooding and tornado threats as it moved inland, forecasters and officials warned.
Hurricane-force winds in the Florida panhandle blew the roof off a Pensacola hotel, and the city’s mayor said the airport “took some damage”. The storm flattened a boathouse in Destin and ripped away part of the facade of a high-rise in Panama City Beach.
A worker in a condominium parking lot swept piles of the building’s insulation while others put back beach chairs that had been tossed about.
“Remember, there can still be flooding from rising rivers,” Jared W Perdue, the secretary of Florida’s state transportation department, said at a news conference. “I’m just going to remind all of you – please, if there’s standing water or flowing water on top of a road, please do not drive through it.
“It does not have to be that deep, and it can wash away your car, it can wash away a human, it can become very dangerous very quickly.”
Nearly 550,000 customers were still without power across Florida, Alabama and Georgia on Saturday afternoon as those in the path of the storm began the cleanup process, according to PowerOutage .us . Though still high, the number of outages was down from more than 900,000 earlier on Saturday.
Storm surge and tropical storm warnings associated with Isaias by then had been discontinued, the National Hurricane Center (NHC) warned there would still likely be “considerable impacts” associated with Isaias across much of southern Alabama, Florida’s panhandle and south-western Georgia .
“Flash, urban and river flooding is possible across the region,” the NHC said in a Saturday-morning advisory, adding that there was a considerable potential for flash flooding and landslides across the southern Appalachians. “A risk for tornadoes will persist … through [Saturday] afternoon across parts of the eastern Florida panhandle, Georgia and the Carolinas.”
Isaias through Sunday is expected to produce rainfall amounts of 4-8in across southern Alabama, Florida’s panhandle and Big Bend regions, and south-west Georgia. Localized totals up to 15in are possible, particularly within rain bands across the Florida panhandle and Big Bend.
Across much of the remainder of the south-east US, rainfall amounts of 2-5in are expected, and localized higher amounts up to 10in are possible, especially across the southern Appalachians and coastal Carolinas.
The hurricane’s maximum sustained winds were 105mph (169km/h). That was intense enough to sound like “a train whistle”, Tim Mowry told the Associated Press after enduring the storm as his home in Pensacola, Florida.
after newsletter promotion
Mowry described losing power on Friday afternoon but said could rely on a generator. He said his son tried to drive to his home after his place about 15 minutes away lost power but had to turn around because downed trees and power lines blocked the road.
All things considered, Mowry said he was “really fortunate” with respect to how he fared during Isaias.
Along Alabama’s Gulf coast, authorities in Mobile reported numerous downed trees and power lines.
Maranie Adams, who rode out the storm with her family and their chickens in Gulf Shores, Alabama, said the winds rocked their home, but it was nothing like Hurricane Sally, which left water under their elevated house.
“I feel very much more relieved today,” she said.
Donald Trump has allowed the Federal Emergency Management Agency (Fema) to provide resources to Georgia to help grapple with the ongoing storm, including possible tornadoes, the agency said on Saturday.
Several roads have already been blocked by fallen trees around Atlanta, local outlets have reported.
Trump previously approved emergency declarations for Florida and Alabama ahead of the landfall of Hurricane Isaias .
While the stronger El Niño seemed to limit the number of hurricanes in the Atlantic for the year so far, Isaias forming in October with maximum sustained winds of 105mph marked a stark contrast from historical trends.
The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (Noaa) predicted a quiet year in terms of hurricanes at the beginning of a season that officially begins annually on 1 June. Noaa anticipated between three and six hurricanes, well below the average of seven. An August forecast from Noaa cut the expected number to between two and six.
Isais is one of the two latest-forming Atlantic hurricanes on record, tying a record set on 8 October 1905. Otherwise, the second-latest date for the first Atlantic hurricane was 11 September – in 2002 and 2013.
None of the eight previous named storms of the 2026 Atlantic season intensified above tropical storm status.
The Associated Press contributed reporting

articles.title_orig: Pope criticizes death penalty after Hegseth announces public execution
articles.title_zh: Pope criticizes death penalty after Hegseth announces public execution
articles.content_orig:
ROME — Pope Leo XIV on Saturday declared capital punishment “inadmissible” as he marked the World Day Against the Death Penalty and his native United States announced plans to livestream an execution by firing squad.
In a post on X, the American pope quoted the revised Catholic teaching on capital punishment ushered in by Pope Francis that the death penalty attacks the inherent dignity of a human being.
“The common good can be safeguarded and the requirements of justice can be met without recourse to capital punishment,” read the post under Leo’s official handle, @Pontifex. “Effective systems of detention have been developed that protect citizens while at the same time do not completely deprive those who are guilty of the possibility of redemption.”
The post ended with the hashtag #NoDeathPenalty.
The U.S. Defense Department announced Thursday that the firing squad execution of Nidal Malik Hasan, convicted of a 2009 shooting at the Fort Hood military base, will be livestreamed. Hasan, scheduled to be executed at Fort Hood on Dec. 3, was convicted of killing 13 people and wounding 32 others.
Why Hegseth's decision to livestream execution is raising questions
Leo didn’t refer specifically to the planned execution, or the botched lethal injection in Tennessee last week that has revived debate over the death penalty in the United States. Saturday is World Day Against the Death Penalty, and it is common for the pope’s official social media accounts to post messages marking such commemorations.
But Leo’s post came just hours after his top deputy, Cardinal Pietro Parolin, the Vatican secretary of state, said explicitly that the planned U.S. public execution was “unacceptable.”
Pope Francis in 2018 amended official Catholic teaching to declare capital punishment “inadmissible” in all circumstances.
Previously, the Catechism of the Catholic Church, the official compendium of church teaching, said the church didn’t exclude recourse to capital punishment “if this is the only possible way of effectively defending human lives against the unjust aggressor.”
Past popes had upheld that position, though St. John Paul II began urging an end to the practice and stressed that guilty people were just as deserving of dignity as innocent ones.
Like Francis before him, Leo has made visiting prisons a key part of his papal travel in a bid to give a message of hope to inmates and underscore their inherent dignity, that God loves them and that there is always a chance for redemption.
“If any of you fear being abandoned by everyone, know that God will never abandon you, and that the church will stand by your side,” Leo told inmates at the notorious Bata prison in Equatorial Guinea during his visit in April. Leo is to visit a prison in Buenos Aires during his upcoming tour through Latin America.
Pope Leo asked if he helped with historic White Sox turnaround
Speaking specifically about the United States, Cardinal Pietro Parolin, the Vatican secretary of state, said the planned livestreamed execution was “truly incomprehensible” and “unacceptable to turn death into a spectacle.”
“The Church’s position is one of total opposition to the death penalty; it is incompatible with human dignity and serves as no deterrent—,” Parolin said in comments carried by Vatican News. “It is truly incomprehensible that anyone would want to use this system today — I don’t know for what purpose. It is certainly unacceptable to turn death into a spectacle; even if the person is guilty, of course, there are other methods.”
The head of the U.S. bishops conference, Archbishop Paul Coakley, expressed “shock” and “great sorrow” at the Pentagon’s plans.
“In no way can Hasan’s actions be condoned but this decision is a barbaric promotion of a culture of death and must be reconsidered,” he said in a statement Friday. “The public execution even of one who has done grave harm will only further undermine the moral fabric of our nation and be a blight on the conscience of its people.”

articles.title_orig: It's 'probably not plausible' that a strong economy can steady U.S. debt as 5%-6% growth is needed
articles.title_zh: It's 'probably not plausible' that a strong economy can steady U.S. debt as 5%-6% growth is needed
articles.content_orig:
Congressional Budget Office Director Phillip Swagel said faster economic growth is unlikely to keep U.S. debt in check, even if GDP expands at more than double its current pace.
Gross debt is now $40 trillion, and publicly held debt is 100% of GDP. Just keeping that ratio flat, let alone bringing it down, would require a massive, sustained boom. For now, CBO see the debt-to-GDP ratio soaring to 120% by 2036.
During a Minneapolis Fed conference on Thursday, Swagel said stronger economic growth will help by bringing in more revenue for the federal government, but it’s not that simple.
Federal spending also boosts growth, which lifts wages that in turn affect outlays on Social Security benefits, he pointed out. A robust economy also tends to send interest rates higher, which adds to debt interest costs.
“So growth will help, but it’s probably not plausible that growth alone will stabilize our fiscal trajectory,” Swagel added. “So then we’re left with changes in revenues and changes in spending, and those are inherently political choices.”
Minneapolis Fed President Neel Kashkari asked if AI can help supercharge economic growth, and he replied that CBO has detected an increase in total factor productivity, which measures the efficiency of labor, capital, and other inputs.
The CBO’s next batch of economic forecasts due early next year will incorporate its views on AI, Swagel said, adding that future growth will be stronger. Still, the budget deficit is so deep that even the extra AI-powered growth won’t be enough, he warned.
Kashkari then asked how much faster growth would have to be in order to stabilize the debt. Swagel cautioned against doing arithmetic on the fly but offered some back-of-the-envelope numbers.
Assuming interest rates of 4%-5%, he estimated that nominal GDP growth would have to reach 7%-8% and real GDP growth would have to hit 5%-6%.
That’s more than double the latest real GDP pace of 2.2% in the second quarter. Meanwhile, even bullish Wall Street forecasts put full-year GDP growth at 2.5%.
The rough numbers from the CBO chief also far exceed what Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said would be needed to overcome the debt.
“With 3% growth, we grow our way out of this,” he said at Southern Methodist University last month. “We’ll get to the other side of this Iran conflict, and the underlying economy is very, very strong, and I think reaccelerating.”
Meanwhile, other estimates fall somewhere in between. According to the Penn Wharton Budget Model, growth would have to average 3.5%-4% over a decade to maintain the debt-to-GDP ratio.
Swagel also noted that an economic shock that sends interest rates up suddenly would set off a vicious fiscal cycle.
“So there’s almost like a turbocharger,” he explained. “An interest rate shock feeds into the deficit, feeds into the debt, feeds back into interest rates.”
So far, the bond market is absorbing all the debt the U.S. Treasury is issuing to fund the budget deficit, but long-term yields have surged to the highest levels in 24 years.
Some of that is due to the strong economy, expectations for Fed rate hikes, high oil prices keeping inflation high, and the flood of AI hyperscaler debt competing for bond market demand.
But the enormous scale of U.S. debt is also a factor. Swagel said it’s small now, with a 1-percentage-point increase in the debt ratio leading to a 0.015-percentage-point hike on long-term interest rates.
“So it’s modest, but the fiscal trajectory is really quite challenging,” he added. “It adds up, and of course there’s that turbocharger type effect that I mentioned where it feeds back into deficits.”
Jason Ma is the weekend editor at Fortune , where he covers markets, the economy, finance, and housing.

articles.title_orig: Tropical Storm Rachel's surf drives out Long Beach residents, briefly shuts Newport Beach beaches
articles.title_zh: Tropical Storm Rachel's surf drives out Long Beach residents, briefly shuts Newport Beach beaches
articles.content_orig:
This is read by an automated voice. Please report any issues or inconsistencies here .
See more from the L.A. Times in Google Search. Set us as preferred
A coastal flood warning covered beaches from Malibu to San Diego on Saturday as Tropical Storm Rachel moved toward Southern California, while Long Beach kept some oceanfront residents under an evacuation order, and Newport Beach closed piers and temporarily shuttered beaches before a reopening.
“There is growing confidence that the expected coastal flooding impacts on Sunday morning for vulnerable south-facing beaches of LA County could be the most significant we have seen so far this season, including those seen with Marie,” the National Weather Service’s Oxnard office said Saturday.
Its San Diego office said Sunday morning would carry the highest flooding risks along the Orange and San Diego coasts as swells, onshore winds and high tides combine.
The center of Rachel was expected to move onshore in northern Baja California on Saturday night, the National Hurricane Center said.
Those warnings remained in effect even as Rachel’s forecast track shifted farther south, leaving most of San Diego County outside its projected path, said Adam Roser, lead meteorologist at the National Weather Service in San Diego. “Even though the track has shifted a little farther to the south, we’re still expecting wind impacts,” Roser said during a briefing.
A tropical storm watch remained in effect for all of San Diego County, the weather service said.
Long Beach’s mandatory order covers homes on Seaside Walk between 64th and 66th places. It took effect at 7 p.m. Friday and runs through noon Tuesday, city officials said. A commercial crane is scheduled to drop sandbags on 65th Place and westward in front of addresses between 65th and 64th, city officials said.
“The return date is subject to change based on evolving conditions,” a city announcement said.
Waves topped the bulkhead and sent water into homes and streets, according to city officials. Inspectors red-tagged eight buildings across 13 addresses, including apartments, and yellow-tagged at least one, Mayor Rex Richardson said Saturday. A red tag marks a building as unsafe to enter, and a yellow tag restricts its use.
The city closed the Peninsula to nonresident traffic, with more street closures starting at 62nd Place.
Richardson urged residents to “take this seriously and be prepared.” Todd Leland, a manager in the Long Beach Parks, Recreation and Marine Department, said the city’s bulkhead and pedestrian boardwalk had already sustained significant structural damage.
Workers are bracing damaged sections with timber and thousands of sandbags to stabilize the compromised areas and prevent collapse.
“Prepare right now for the impacts,” Richardson said. “Our infrastructure was not built for this.”
Long Beach City Manager Tom Modica said that he expected a lengthy recovery. “We will be asking for assistance from the governor, and potentially also from the federal government,” Modica said. “We don’t think this is just going to be this weekend. This is going to be the entire next couple of months.”
Water at the Los Angeles Harbor tide gauge peaked at 7.7 feet Saturday morning, about 1.6 feet above the predicted tide, the National Weather Service said. “The projected high tides of around 8 feet for Sunday morning would approach or exceed recent record tide levels for L.A. County,” it said.
In Newport Beach, police posted an alert online Saturday morning saying flooding closed all city beaches and piers until further notice.
“Stay away from these areas,” police said. The announcement followed Newport Beach declaring a local emergency Friday after overnight flooding on the Balboa Peninsula.
By early afternoon, police said the beaches were open, but Newport Pier, Balboa Pier and the Wedge, from the rock jetty to M Street, remained closed.
In a video uploaded to the city’s Instagram account, an official asked people to stay off the berms. The man said the flooding would continue over the next couple of days. “We want the public to be safe during this time. We will get through this,” his post said.
The weather service expects more coastal flooding Sunday, when high tide at Newport Beach is forecast to reach 7.6 feet at 9:48 a.m. “Low-lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure may flood,” the agency’s San Diego office said. Surf could reach 6 to 9 feet, highest at south-facing beaches, especially in Orange County, Roser said.
Joe Angelo has lived in the Newport Beach area for 60 years and bought his beachfront home 27 years ago. He said the flooding left him in “shock and disbelief.”
“I haven’t seen one drop of water on that sand in 27 years. All the sand, not one drop of water,” Angelo said. “We all love living on this oceanfront. But, boy, it makes you think twice.”
Sandbags lined dozens of homes and businesses near Balboa Boulevard on Saturday morning. Beachgoers strolled with coffee in hand, went for morning runs and walked their dogs. Despite the warnings, many climbed sand berms to watch the waves. Some did backflips off the sand.
Chris Perkins of Orange County brought his son Connor to see the surf. “I grew up around the ocean, and [I’m] just trying to expose my kid to the gnarly waves, and show him how to be safe and how to do it the right way,” Perkins said.
In Long Beach, cars lined up Saturday at a Peninsula parking lot as fire department workers loaded sandbags into trunks. Light rain began falling shortly before noon.
Monica Shephard, who lives in a beachfront apartment complex, said she was worried, noting that ocean water reached her doorstep three years ago. She planned to pick up sandbags for her complex Saturday night and praised the city’s precautions. “They’re doing a great job,” she said.
Huntington Beach also activated its emergency operations center Friday, the city said. Many spectators watched pounding waves there at high tide Saturday morning. Cyclists, walkers and runners packed the white concrete trail along Bolsa Chica State Beach. A section that flooded Friday appeared to escape more trouble Saturday, despite signs that said “flooded.”
The heaviest rain is expected late Saturday night into Sunday morning, Roser said. Most coastal areas could get about an inch or a little less. Some mountain areas could get more than four inches.
Many areas west of the mountains will stay in the 60s on Monday, and Big Bear may only reach the 40s, Roser said. Temperatures should warm by the end of the week, he said.
Inland, southern San Bernardino County faces at least a 40% chance of excessive rain that could result in flash flooding through Saturday night, said Julie Phillipson, lead meteorologist at the National Weather Service in Las Vegas. “Our primary concern is still the heavy rains and the flooding that can occur.”
Deputy Managing Editor Shelby Grad contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: WHO says no plague case registered after Russian lab worker’s death
articles.title_zh: WHO says no plague case registered after Russian lab worker’s death
articles.content_orig:
The World Health Organization (WHO) has said it still does not know what caused the pneumonia that killed a laboratory worker at a Russian plague research institute and that no case of plague has been registered.
Russia’s state health regulator told the WHO that tests on the worker and people who had been in contact with her were negative for the dangerous pathogens they tested for, the United Nations health agency said in a statement on Saturday.
Her contacts still showed no symptoms, and no further linked cases of severe pneumonia had been found, the WHO added.
“Based on the information provided… WHO has not identified evidence of ongoing transmission associated with this event. A key uncertainty remains the absence of a confirmed diagnosis in the deceased laboratory worker,” it said.
The worker fell ill and died in undisclosed circumstances on October 2, prompting authorities to quarantine about 200 people and stoking public health fears on social media.
Russian media named her as Darya Shipilova, a 28-year-old laboratory technician at the Irkutsk Antiplague Research Institute of Siberia and the Far East, in the Siberian region of Irkutsk.
Pneumonic plague, a lung infection caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis, which is usually found in small mammals and their fleas, was suspected early on.
The governor of neighbouring Buryatia said the woman had “died, maybe of the plague”.
Russia’s health watchdog Rospotrebnadzor said she had been diagnosed with “pneumonia of unknown aetiology”.
Russian authorities said the worker was appropriately vaccinated and that no microorganisms linked to her work were found in her body. They say post-mortem tests did not detect plague.
On Thursday, Russia said it had completed health checks on all her contacts and had given the WHO all the information.
A local official said on October 6 that 60 percent of those placed in quarantine had already been released.
WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus asked Russia on Wednesday to respond to media reports of a second employee with pneumonia of undetermined cause. Russia dismissed the reports as “false information”.
The United States has also called on Russia for transparency.
Global health officials have been extra alert to deadly pneumonia cases of unknown cause since the COVID-19 pandemic, which began with a cluster of fast-spreading, fatal respiratory illness in China.
The cause of individual pneumonia cases often cannot be determined.

articles.title_orig: Some Republicans Reject Trump’s Move to Import Diesel Fuel From Russia
articles.title_zh: Some Republicans Reject Trump’s Move to Import Diesel Fuel From Russia
articles.content_orig:
President Donald Trump 's Friday announcement that Russia will supply diesel fuel to the global market marked an apparent pivot from recent efforts to pressure Moscow to end the Ukraine war by targeting Russian energy exports.
Trump claimed the move, unveiled with less than a month left in an affordability-focused midterm election , would swiftly bring down record-high diesel prices .
But commentators and critics were quick to highlight contradictions between the new policy and prior efforts by the U.S. to clamp down on Russian oil sales.
Those efforts most recently included the enactment of the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 , empowering Trump to impose tariffs up to 100% on the top purchasers of Russian crude oil or gas, among other restrictions. Trump signed the bill into law just three weeks ago .
"Congress just passed a law giving Trump the power to impose new tariffs on major buyers of Russian oil & gas," Scott Lincicome, vice president of the libertarian Cato Institute, said on X after Trump's Friday announcement.
"Can America tariff America?" he quipped.
Sen. Richard Blumenthal , D-Conn., a member of the Senate Ukraine Caucus, accused Trump's latest move of being "directly contrary to Congress's intent in our bipartisan sanctions bill."
Peter Harrell, visiting scholar at Georgetown University Law Center's Institute of International Economic Law, in an X post said that the relaxation of Russian diesel restrictions "pretty much proves the point that the Graham Russia Bill was not going to force the Trump Administration to increase economic pressure on Moscow."
Some of the criticism crossed party lines.
"Through the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, we gave the president significant authorities and leverage against China and Russia to bring Putin's war to an end with a negotiated settlement," Rep. Michael McCaul, R-Texas, said in an X post. "Unfortunately, while I understand the desire to bring down diesel prices, I am concerned the lifting of sanctions on Russian oil will only fund the Kremlin's war machine—emboldening more violence and destruction, as we have seen in recent days," McCaul said.
The White House did not immediately respond to CNBC's questions about the diesel agreement with Russia.
Less than a year earlier, the Trump administration slapped sanctions on multiple Russian oil companies in response to what it called "Russia's lack of serious commitment to a peace process to end the war in Ukraine."
Trump also had previously slammed NATO allies for continuing to buy Russian oil. In a September 2025 Truth Social post , he wrote, "the purchase of Russian Oil, by some, has been shocking! It greatly weakens your negotiating position, and bargaining power, over Russia."
Later that month, Trump again harangued world leaders for doing business with Russia.
"They're funding the war against themselves. Who the hell ever heard of that one?" he said in a speech at the United Nations General Assembly. "They can't be doing what they're doing. They're buying oil and gas from Russia while they're fighting Russia."
Trump announced the diesel deal in a Truth Social post Friday afternoon after what he described as a "highly successful discussion" with Russian President Vladimir Putin .
Under the agreement, Russia will immediately supply more than 300,000 tons of diesel, then another 500,000 tons in November, followed by 1 million tons "immediately thereafter" and 3 million more depending on refinery conditions, Trump wrote.
The Treasury Department soon after said that Trump directed the Office of Foreign Assets Control to immediately issue a "temporary general license to allow the supply of Russian diesel to the global market." OFAC specified that the sanctioned transactions will be authorized for about six months, until April 7.
Russia seemed to celebrate the move. "Russia-US cooperation on diesel and energy will benefit the world," an X account associated with Putin's economic envoy Kirill Dmitriev said in response to the announcement.
But Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskyy , whose military has started targeting Russian oil refineries, said in a searing statement that the U.S. easing sanctions on Moscow "plays into Russia's hands."
"Any easing of sanctions against Russia without a clear and lasting de-escalation agreement with Russia is an obvious weakness," Zelenskyy said. "Allowing Russia to sell petroleum products is an investment in a war that must be ended, not prolonged."
"We count on America's fair support for our defense of life, for our defense of people in Ukraine – and on the United States having a correspondingly strong conversation with Russia," he said.
"A strong one, not a weak one," he added.
Trump thanked Putin later Friday afternoon for enabling "massive amounts of oil" to come to the U.S.
"We need oil for the world, and this is diesel, which is what we need, so we're very happy to get it," Trump told reporters before heading to Syracuse, New York.
The Trump administration has previously eased some Russian energy sanctions temporarily, though more narrowly than Friday's announcement.
Earlier this year, in an attempt to stabilize markets after the start of the Iran war, the Trump administration issued limited, 30-day waivers allowing countries to buy sanctioned Russian oil that was already in transit.
But some interpreted the latest move as a more significant step.
"It looks like Trump cut a deal with the devil," Jeremy Siegel, professor emeritus of finance at the Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania, told CNBC's " Closing Bell " Friday afternoon.
"It's not a permanent solution at all. It's sort of a short-term Band Aid," Siegel said. "And cutting back on or eliminating sanctions on Russia for the invasion in Ukraine, I think, is a very unfortunate consequence."
