Video taken in cities including Paris, Lyon and Strasbourg showed demonstrators facing off with police, lighting fires and dodging tear gas. France’s interior ministry said over 6,000 people had been taken into custody.
French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu defended the police response to student protests after one teenager lost a hand in an incident involving a police grenade and another lost sight in one eye after being struck by a projectile.
In parliament on Tuesday, Lecornu pushed back on accusations of police brutality or state repression, adding that the term "police brutality" implies that officers had been instructed to use force, according to Politico.
"What triggers police action is the occurrence of urban violence," Lecornu said.
"Can accidents happen? The answer is yes," he added.
FRANCE EXPLODES AGAIN AS STUDENTS RIOT OVER EDUCATION
French riot police stand near burning objects during clashes with protesters in Paris on Tuesday, Oct. 6, 2026. (Reuters)
Lecornu and Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez have both argued that the police response was sparked by urban violence, arson and vandalism, while maintaining that officers have acted within their authority. Nuñez also called the police response proportionate in "almost all cases."
The prime minister also accused opposition party France Unbowed of exploiting the student protests to sow chaos and score political points ahead of next year’s presidential election.
President Emmanuel Macron convened an emergency meeting with senior ministers to address the nationwide student protests and their potential political fallout.
The French government is facing mounting pressure after more than 6,500 people were arrested and hundreds were injured as students demand better funding and learning conditions in schools. Most of those arrested were minors, according to The Associated Press.
Riot police use a water cannon as they face students during a protest against under-resourced schools in Rennes, western France, on Tuesday, Oct. 6, 2026. (Jeremias Gonzalez/AP)
Lecornu said 215 students and 85 school staff members had been injured since the protests began, while his office said 715 police officers had also been injured.
"I hope we can provide a political response to a very real anxiety among high school students," Lecornu acknowledged.
As Lecornu delivered his remarks on Tuesday, demonstrators from several French unions and teachers’ groups gathered with high school and university students. Members of France’s left-wing parties were also at the protest, according to Politico.
The Interior Ministry estimated that 266,000 people took part in demonstrations nationwide Tuesday, including 56,000 in Paris.
The Paris demonstration was largely peaceful, although smaller groups later clashed with riot police, according to The Associated Press.
The protesters' movement began at high schools in the Paris region in mid-September before spreading nationwide.
TEEN'S HAND BLOWN OFF BY POLICE GRENADE DURING FRENCH STUDENT PROTESTS: REPORT
French riot police officers remove elements of a burning street barricade during a demonstration by French high school and university students in Lyon on Oct. 6, 2026. (Reuters)

On Monday, a 15-year-old boy in northern France lost a hand after a police grenade exploded during the protests, Politico reported. A prosecutor said he could not "say for certain whether the student picked up the grenade or whether it was thrown at him."
In the city of Tours, a 16-year-old lost sight in one eye after being hit by a projectile, according to the outlet. The prosecutor said the projectile may have been fired from a sub-lethal riot-control weapon used by police.
Boris Vallaud, leader of the center-left Socialist group in parliament, said the group's lawmakers would introduce legislation restricting the use of sub-lethal riot-control weapons at student demonstrations, warning that they can cause irreversible injuries, the outlet reported.

articles.title_zh: 9 dead, including children, in mass shooting in Erie, Pennsylvania
articles.content_orig:
Nine people, including children and a gunman, were killed in a mass shooting in Erie, Pennsylvania, officials said.
A man killed eight people including a pregnant woman, children and other relatives at his home in Erie, Pennsylvania, before taking his own life as well, authorities said Saturday.
Police first responded to a home on Perry Street in Erie on Friday, Oct. 9, around 5 p.m., after witnesses reported seeing a gunman firing shots outside the house before entering the residence.
Stream Philadelphia News for free, 24/7, wherever you are with NBC10.
When police arrived, they found two women who had been shot to death in the street.
The shooting escalated into a standoff as Erie Police and SWAT teams surrounded the home. More shots were then heard inside the home. When police entered, they found the bodies of seven other people, including children, as well as the gunman who died from what appeared to be a self-inflicted gunshot wound, according to investigators.
Erie Police Chief Rick Lorah described the incident as one of the most difficult and heartbreaking scenes he had ever encountered.
“The loss of life is devastating and the circumstances we are working through are deeply disturbing,” Chief Lorah said. “At this time, we can confirm that the suspect is deceased. Based on the information currently available to us, there is no ongoing threat to the public. Our hearts are with the victims, their families, and everyone affected by this tragedy. There are no words that can be adequately express the magnitude of the loss of life here.”
Investigators are currently working to determine what led to the shooting.

“We will not speculate about a motive, or at least information that could compromise this investigation,” Chief Lorah said. “It's just a devastating loss of life. It's a terrible, terrible scene at this point, and we just need time to piece together what happened here.”

articles.title_orig: U.S. measles cases surpass 4,000, with over 25 percent coming from Pennsylvania
articles.title_zh: U.S. measles cases surpass 4,000, with over 25 percent coming from Pennsylvania
articles.content_orig:
A list of frequently asked questions about this highly contagious virus.
Pennsylvania is grappling with its biggest measles outbreak in three decades, with the most deaths reported in the nation in a single year since 1992.
Here are answers to frequently asked questions about this highly contagious virus, according to federal, state, and local health agency resources and advisories.
Measles is spread through the air, from an infected person. The virus can linger in the air and on surfaces for up to two hours. People can become infected if they inhale contaminated air, or touch a contaminated surface and then their eyes, nose, or mouth.
Measles is the most contagious virus known to humans. Nine out of 10 unvaccinated people who come into contact with measles will get sick.
The most common signs of measles include high fever, cough, runny nose, watery eyes, and a blotchy rash. Severe complications are rare but can include pneumonia, brain swelling, and neurological problems. About one out of every 1,000 measles patients develop acute encephalitis — brain swelling that can lead to permanent brain damage, according to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. About one to three out of every 1,000 measles patients die from complications.
Infants and children under age 5 are at high risk, and adults can also experience serious complications. So can pregnant women and people with weakened immune systems.
Individuals in these groups who are unvaccinated — for instance, infants who are too young to receive the vaccine and people being treated for cancer who can’t be vaccinated — are particularly vulnerable. But the virus can cause severe complications even among people who are otherwise healthy.
Measles is contagious for an eight-day window: four days before rash symptoms appear, through four days after. Symptoms typically appear within seven to 14 days after exposure, but can take up to 21 days. So a person with no rash can still be contagious.
A measles rash starts as flat red spots on the face near a person’s hairline. It usually appears three to five days after a person develops early symptoms linked with a variety of illnesses, like a fever, a cough or a runny nose, according to the CDC .
The rash then spreads downward across the body. A person might also have small, raised bumps on top of the flat red spots, the CDC says, and the spots might appear to join together as they spread.
Get vaccinated. Two doses of the measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine offer 97% protection against measles, making it the most effective way to avoid getting sick.
Unvaccinated people who have already been exposed to measles can get an MMR shot within 72 hours of the exposure, which may provide protection against the virus. Patients who are vaccinated may experience a milder illness if they do develop measles, the CDC says .
In some cases, people at high risk of severe disease can take an antibody treatment, immune globulin, within six days of exposure. After a measles exposure in a neonatal intensive care unit at Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia, infants there who were too young to be vaccinated received preventive antibody treatments .
While immune globulin may offer some protection, no specific treatment has been developed for measles.
Chances are low, because the vaccine is so effective. So-called breakthrough infections in vaccinated people occur in about 3% of cases. Vaccinated individuals who are in areas with widespread measles cases are at greater risk.
In September, Pennsylvania officials reported four people who were appropriately vaccinated and still contracted measles. None required hospitalization and the cases represent less than 1% of the total measles cases reported in the state this year.
Leading physicians’ groups and the CDC recommend children receive the first dose of the measles vaccine at one year of age, and a second dose before entering kindergarten, around age 5. The vaccine is among those required to attend school, though a growing number of families have legally opted out for various reasons.
In Pennsylvania, doctors have begun recommending a “dose zero” for children who are at least six months old, and accelerated shots for kids over 1, if they live in an area with an active measles outbreak.
» READ MORE: More Philly-area classrooms are seeing lower measles vaccination rates. How protected is your school?
Most adults who are fully vaccinated or considered immune from a childhood infection do not need a booster. But people who live in an area with high measles transmission may want to get tested for measles antibody levels.
A titer test measures antibodies in the blood of people who are immune to the virus either from vaccination or past infection. People with low levels of antibodies may benefit from a booster shot.
Since measles has no direct treatment, options focus on managing symptoms. Mild, flulike symptoms can be treated with rest, hydration, and over-the-counter pain relievers.
People who have measles should isolate themselves for at least four days after developing a rash, and caretakers should wear an N95 mask while in the same room.
More severe measles complications, such as difficulty breathing, pneumonia, severe dehydration, or extremely high fever require hospital care.
Chickenpox, or varicella, is caused by a different virus, the varicella-zoster virus. It is less contagious than measles, the CDC says, but can still infect about 90% of unvaccinated people who come into close contact with a person with chickenpox.
A measles rash is flat and blotchy and starts on the forehead, while a chickenpox rash begins with red spots on the chest , stomach, face, and back that then turn into itchy blisters that eventually scab. Once all sores have scabbed, the person is no longer contagious.
Rubella, sometimes called “German measles,” is not caused by the measles virus. No longer common in the United States, it’s particularly dangerous for pregnant women and can cause serious birth defects or miscarriage, the CDC says .
Most people who get measles recover without serious complications.
But about one in five unvaccinated people who get measles must be hospitalized, as seen this year in Pennsylvania’s outbreak. Additionally, up to one in 20 children with measles will develop pneumonia, and one in 1,000 children will develop swelling of the brain, according to the CDC.
Getting measles during pregnancy can contribute to a premature birth, low birth weight, and even miscarriage or infant mortality.
Measles can also put patients at a higher risk from other infections, an effect known as “immune amnesia” that can last months or years, the CDC says.
Pennsylvania health officials have reported five measles-associated deaths in the current outbreak.
The state defines a “measles-associated death” as one that occurs within 30 days of symptom onset in a person with clinical evidence of infection and a positive laboratory test, and who did not die of another unrelated cause, like a car crash.
Pennsylvania health officials update a dashboard tracking measles cases three times a week, so you can check to find out if there are measles cases in your county.
The MMR vaccine is widely available and usually covered by insurance. Call your pediatrician or primary care provider, or your local pharmacy. The vaccine is also offered at Federally Qualified Health Centers , state-run health centers , and county health departments .
Call your healthcare provider if you think you have measles. They can test you through a blood test, a urine sample, or a nose or throat swab. Healthcare providers can call the state health department at 877-724-3258, or contact their local health department, to report a case of suspected measles or ask questions about testing.
Call your healthcare provider or the state health department’s toll-free hotline at 877-PA-HEALTH (877-724-3258) if you think you were exposed to measles and have symptoms.

articles.title_orig: House candidate who reported rape on campaign trail on why she came forward: "What about all the women who are victims?"
articles.title_zh: House candidate who reported rape on campaign trail on why she came forward: "What about all the women who are victims?"
articles.content_orig:
In the days since U.S. House candidate Bernadette Greene-Placentia publicly came forward alleging she was raped over the summer while repairing a campaign sign, she says women have been reaching out to her to share their own stories.
"The humbling thing is that so many – hundreds and hundreds of women from around the world — have taken the time to write me and tell me their own story," Greene-Placentia told CBS News in an interview. "I would say about 70% of them have acknowledged that they never reported it, and they are thanking me for being in the public eye and talking about it and giving voice because they didn't feel like they had a voice when they went through the same thing."
Greene-Placentia, a Democrat, is facing freshman Republican Rep. Abe Hamadeh on the ballot in November in Arizona's 8th District, located in the Phoenix suburbs. The district is rated as solidly Republican by Cook Political Report.
The reported sexual assault happened amid a heated campaign season, as concerns about political violence swirl. At a rally in September, an armed man lunged at Ohio gubernatorial candidate Amy Acton, and at a town hall earlier this year, a man lunged and sprayed vinegar at Rep. Ilhan Omar.
Greene-Placentia, who had been a long-haul trucker, told CBS News that "we are not a well-funded campaign," and she and her staff were usually the ones putting up campaign signs or fixing them.
"I took pride in being able to, you know, do these things myself because we are a grassroots campaign, so it wasn't unusual," she said of fixing signs at all hours.
She said that a "little after midnight" one night in August, she was repairing some supplies when she was hit on the back of the head. When she regained consciousness, she said she realized she was on the ground, and a "man was on top of me, and then I felt pain down there." She said that man "climbed off," and then another man assaulted her.
"At that point, I remember I started, like, moving around and kicking," she said. "He said, 'You know, just not worth it.' And they left. I don't know how long I stayed there."
Greene-Placentia said she drove straight home, and she said she believes police have footage of her driving home.
A police report from the Maricopa County Sheriff's Office says the incident occurred on Aug. 14 between 2 a.m. and 3 a.m., and she reported the incident on Aug. 31.
The Maricopa County Sheriff's Office said in a statement earlier this week that it was investigating the incident but could not comment further.
Greene-Placentia said she told her husband and staff the next day, but she didn't want to talk about it at first.
Greene-Placentia said Friday that she realized she wanted to come forward while she was telling her own personal story on the trail. She said she was talking about how her father died while waiting to get care with the Department of Veterans Affairs and she found out six months later that her mother had been rationing her insulin.
"I was asking them, 'Do you think anybody's gonna fight harder than me?'" Greene-Placentia said. "And then in the back of my head, I'm like, 'Well you're telling these folks that you're gonna fight for them, but what about all the women that are victims of sexual assault? Are you not gonna fight for them? That kind of makes you a hypocrite, Bernadette.'"
Greene-Placentia's story was first published on Wednesday in the Phoenix New Times. Since then, her opponent, Hamadeh, called it a "disturbing story," and he was calling "upon authorities to investigate these serious allegations thoroughly, including finding all possible camera footage of the time and place in order to prosecute the crime to the fullest extent of the law."
Greene-Placentia said that she wants to tell women who come up to her that she understands what they are going through.
"As women, we want to take responsibility for everything and blame ourselves, and that is a societal problem we've got to get away from," Greene-Placentia said.

articles.title_orig: Hundreds of doctors demand World Medical Association suspend Israel
articles.title_zh: Hundreds of doctors demand World Medical Association suspend Israel
articles.content_orig:
Hundreds of doctors have gathered outside the World Medical Association (WMA) summit in the Netherlands, calling for the suspension of the Israeli Medical Association (IMA) from the grouping of physicians.
On Saturday, 81 healthcare workers removed their scrubs and hung them in a line facing the WMA assembly in Rotterdam, each bearing the name of a Palestinian healthcare worker currently held in illegal Israeli detention.
It was part of a protest against the continued membership of the Israeli association in the WMA, “despite them breaching almost every ethical principle in the WMA’s Code of Medical Ethics”, the IMA Out! coalition that organised the demonstration said in a statement.
“These scrubs should not be empty. Our colleagues belong with their patients, not in Israeli prisons. Today, we literally placed their names at the WMA’s doorstep,” said Mejrem Ahmetaj, a general practitioner and member of IMA Out!.
Since October 2023, Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza has killed more than 1,700 Palestinian healthcare workers and destroyed nearly all the hospitals and healthcare facilities in the enclave.
The campaign accused the Israeli medical association of remaining silent as Palestinian healthcare has been systematically destroyed.
“The IMA is not a bystander. It defends these attacks and blocks international condemnation while Palestinian healthcare is being destroyed. That is not medical neutrality. That is complicity,” added Ahmetaj.
At a meeting of international doctors, medical leaders and human rights activists during the WMA summit on Thursday, the destruction of Palestinian healthcare and the responsibility of the international medical community were discussed, the campaign said.
“Our Palestinian colleagues are being killed and imprisoned, where they are starved and tortured. Their hospitals have been destroyed and patients driven out or murdered. The IMA has said and done nothing about these war crimes against health workers, patients and hospitals,” said a statement by Jonathan Fluxman on behalf of IMA OUT!.
“Thirty years of WMA dialogue with the IMA has done nothing but give the IMA a sense of impunity … It is time for national medical associations and the WMA to speak out and take action. Break your ties with the IMA and suspend the IMA from the WMA now,” he added.
The IMA OUT! campaign said it delivered a petition calling for the IMA’s suspension, signed by more than 6,500 health workers from around the world.
They also demanded accountability for the complicity of Israeli doctors in the starvation, torture and medical neglect of Palestinian prisoners.
Among those held by Israel is Dr Hussam Abu Safia , head of Gaza’s Kamal Adwan Hospital, whose unlawful detention has prompted an international outcry.
He was briefly held at the notorious Sde Teiman detention camp and has been subject to torture and medical neglect. Doctors protesting in Rotterdam held up placards demanding his release.
Abu Safia’s son Elyas, addressing a meeting organised by the campaign, said, “My father and all Palestinian detainees must be treated in accordance with medical ethics, and doctors must abide by the Hippocratic oath they have taken. Care cannot be given based on whose life is deemed worthy.”

articles.title_orig: Protests against voter roll revisions rock capital of world's largest democracy
articles.title_zh: Protests against voter roll revisions rock capital of world's largest democracy
articles.content_orig:
Parts of the capital city of India, the world's largest democracy, are on lockdown. Protests over sweeping revisions to the voter rolls were met with a massive police crackdown.
Parts of the capital of the world's largest democracy are on lockdown tonight. Demonstrations flared across New Delhi today to protest a controversial revision of the country's electoral rolls. Authorities there have removed some 130 million names from voter lists or demanded more proof from residents to stay on the list. The protests took place despite authorities barricading routes and detaining hundreds of demonstrators.
NPR's Diaa Hadid is there, and she is on the line with us now. Talk about what sparked all of this - millions of names being struck off of voter rolls. How did this happen?
DIAA HADID, BYLINE: Yeah, it happened because last year, India's electoral commission announced it would clean up the country's voter rolls by removing people who died, moved addresses or were absent in general. And the ruling Hindu nationalist party, known as the BJP, also pitched it as an effort to root out illegal migrants who they claimed were on the voter rolls.
And there were about 980 million people on those rolls. This is the world's largest democracy. But through the role cleanup, an estimated 130 million names were struck off or were threatened with being removed. And one lawyer litigating against this special role revision is Kaustubh Chaturvedi.
KAUSTUBH CHATURVEDI: It's, by such a wide margin, the largest disenfranchisement that's ever occurred.
HADID: That's ever occurred - now, critics accuse the Hindu nationalist government of trying to disenfranchise India's Muslim minority and other groups unlikely to vote for the ruling party.
ROSE: And in the streets today, Diaa, did authorities try to stop people from protesting at all?
HADID: Yeah, they did. Security forces barricaded the area around the city's designated protest site. They cut off the internet in parts of the city. They even rigged up a loudspeaker blaring recorded warnings.
(SOUNDBITE OF ARCHIVED RECORDING)
UNIDENTIFIED PERSON: Attention, please. Attention, please. Gathering here is not allowed.
HADID: So protesters, mostly young people, kept popping up in different places, and police kept detaining them. One outlet, the Indian Express, reported that some 6,000 people were detained in all. And they included protest leaders who were picked up from their airplane seats right after their flight landed. One lawyer we talked to, who was hiding in a courthouse, told us that dozens of his colleagues were taken away. The lawyer's name is Deepankur. He requested we don't use his family name for his own safety.
DEEPANKUR: I've never noticed such a large-scale detention of lawyers happening. It's unprecedented.
HADID: Unprecedented - that's a word we heard today a lot to describe the authorities' response. And at one intersection, we saw a rush of riot police blowing on whistles.
HADID: They were running towards a young man. It appears he'd shouted a slogan against the government.
(SOUNDBITE OF ARCHIVED RECORDING)
HADID: Where are you taking him? Where are you taking him?
Police were detaining journalists, as well. Many of those arrested were taken to a sports stadium that police were using as a makeshift holding pen. And by the afternoon, protesters ended up gathering on a bridge. They chanted, Delhi belongs to us all, and other slogans of the Indian left.
UNIDENTIFIED PROTESTER: (Chanting in non-English language).
UNIDENTIFIED PROTESTERS: (Chanting in non-English language).
UNIDENTIFIED PROTESTER: (Chanting in non-English language).
UNIDENTIFIED PROTESTERS: (Chanting in non-English language).
ROSE: Wow. That sounds like a chaotic day. How has the government responded to these claims by critics that this is a mass disenfranchisement?
HADID: Well, the electoral commission has issued a statement saying everything they've done is legal, and they urged local officials to check if any voters were incorrectly deleted from the rolls. But the prime minister himself hasn't commented on the situation. Protesters accuse him of hiding behind the police, and they're demanding the resignation of the chief election commissioner.
ROSE: That is NPR's Diaa Hadid in New Delhi. Diaa, thank you, and stay safe.

articles.title_orig: Police officer fatally shot while responding to call in West Philadelphia; DA announces charges
articles.title_zh: Police officer fatally shot while responding to call in West Philadelphia; DA announces charges
articles.content_orig:
10-year police veteran Shane Seiber was killed after responding to a report of a man with a gun
A Philadelphia police officer was fatally shot and another was wounded on Saturday after responding to a report of a man with a gun, authorities said.
Shane Seiber, 40, was killed early on Saturday morning in West Philadelphia , according to the city’s police commissioner, Kevin Bethel.
Seiber, a 10-year veteran of the Philadelphia police department, and the other officer were transported to the Penn Presbyterian medical center, where the surviving officer underwent surgery. He was listed in stable condition, Bethel said.
Bethel also said a suspect was in custody.
Citing law enforcements sources, the Philadelphia Inquirer identified that suspect as Eric Lewis. The Inquirer also reported that Lewis, 35, was employed by Philadelphia’s municipal water department.
Pennsylvania’s governor, Josh Shapiro, said he ordered flags to fly at half-mast for Seiber. He is survived by his wife and two children: a boy, age seven, and a girl, three.
Seiber was at least the 376th Philadelphia police department officer to die in the line of duty since 1851, according to the Officer Down Memorial Page , which honors US law enforcement personnel who died while on the job. He was the 129th of those officers to die from gunfire, the memorial page said.

articles.title_orig: Indian police crack down on 'Cockroach' protest in Delhi
articles.title_zh: Indian police crack down on 'Cockroach' protest in Delhi
articles.content_orig:
The capital of the world’s largest democracy turned into a fortress Saturday, as an extraordinary show of force by Indian authorities met an equally extraordinary display of defiance by the country’s young.
Throughout the day, thousands of people, mostly in their 20s and 30s, tried to gather in Delhi to protest a sweeping revision of their country’s voter roll. Security forces hauled them away, sometimes grabbing them by their arms and legs, and stuffed them, often forcefully, into buses and vans.
Those detained banged on the doors of police vans. They shouted from the windows of buses. One police officer was seen grabbing a protester by the throat. By early evening, more than 2,000 people had been detained, according to a lawyers’ group providing legal aid to the detainees, though an exact number was impossible to ascertain.
The leaders of the Gen Z movement that called for the protest, the Cockroach Janta Party, said they, too, had been detained, including Abhijeet Dipke , one of the movement’s founders.
He shared a video of their encounter with police officers on Instagram. They were landing in Delhi on a flight from Mumbai after attending rallies in other cities earlier in the week, when police officers boarded the plane.
“You can see where the nation is heading. This is dictatorship,” he said. By Saturday evening, it was not known where they were being detained.

Apple revealed in a regulatory filing that it has reached an agreement to bring on team members and technology from personalized audio startup Huxe, in what’s commonly known as a reverse acqui-hire deal.
As first reported in MacRumors , Apple disclosed to the European Commission that it has agreed to make employment offers to “certain employees of Huxe AI,” and to “receive a non-exclusive license to Huxe’s intellectual property rights.”
Reverse acqui-hires emerged in recent years as a way for larger companies to hire key team members and license technology from startups without acquiring the startups outright — presumably allowing them to build up AI talent and tech without drawing as much antitrust scrutiny. (Confusingly, these deals have both been referred to as “reverse acqui-hires” and as plain old “acqui-hires.” )
In the case of Huxe, the startup was founded by developers who’d previously worked on the AI-generated podcast features in NotebookLM (recently renamed Gemini Notebook ). But Huxe announced on May 21 that it was shutting down , with the team posting on the Huxe website that the company would be removing its app from the Apple and Google stores, halting service, and deleting user data.
“The team is moving on to new things, and we won’t be continuing development of the product,” the company said. It also thanked its users, saying, “The fact that you used it, told friends about it, sent us your suggestions and your ideas, made it feel like we built it together.”
On June 9, shortly after Huxe’s announcement, Apple notified the European Commission of its deal.
The filing does not say who received employment offers or if they accepted. Nor does it disclose anything about Apple’s plans.
Possibly related: Huxe’s shutdown announcement came just a day after Spotify unveiled AI-powered podcast generation features of its own , so Apple could be hoping to add similar functionality to its Podcasts app. Tech executives seem enamored with the idea that personalized audio can replace regular podcasts (and maybe even parent-child interaction ?), though it’s not clear how many normal listeners agree.

articles.title_orig: Trump fumes at ‘stain’ on Norway after missing out on Nobel Peace Prize
articles.title_zh: Trump fumes at ‘stain’ on Norway after missing out on Nobel Peace Prize
articles.content_orig:
President complains about not winning prize in year he started war with Iran and says: ‘We will not forget, Norway’
Donald Trump complained on Friday about not winning the Nobel peace prize for 2026, a year in which he started a war with Iran .
At what was supposed to be a rally for other Republican candidates in Syracuse, New York, the US president devoted a long portion of his speech to airing his grievances with the Nobel committee.
“The United States of America, represented by me as your president, should have received the Nobel peace prize , but didn’t. And this is an indelible stain on the country of Norway, and those people that made such a disgraceful and embarrassing decision,” Trump said.
“The Nobel peace prize has been forever discredited by a handful of radical ideologues who are anti-democracy and really enemies of civilization,” Trump went on. “We will not forget, Norway , that you didn’t give this prize.”
Trump also recited a list of wars he claims to have settled, some of which were not wars and some that are still not settled, before adding: “I’m about to settle or win two more: Iran and Russia-Ukraine.”
Trump said he would be ending both wars “quickly”.
“I will tell you what,” he added, darkly. “Iran will be very quick one way or the other: that they give us everything or they don’t exist any longer.”
“Additionally, I stopped Iran from having a nuclear weapon and blowing up the entire Middle East and ultimately far beyond the Middle East, including Europe, perhaps the US and I saved more lives than anyone in history,” Trump claimed, despite the fact that US intelligence agencies reported to Congress in 2025 that Iran had actually suspended its pursuit of nuclear weapons in 2003.
“Despite all of this and all of these unbelievable accomplishments, the Nobel prize was given out today to a liberal person who works at the United Nations, who nobody has ever heard of,” Trump said of Navi Pillay , the South African former UN human rights chief who chaired the UN commission that concluded Israel was guilty of genocide in Gaza.
In Pillay’s first public comments after learning of the award, she joked to colleagues at a conference of human rights lawyers in Nuremberg, Germany, on Friday: “If you clap a little bit more, I may share this prize with Trump.” She then burst out laughing.

articles.title_orig: Ship captains and crews crossing Hormuz earn so much they're 'almost being viewed as mercenaries'
articles.title_zh: Ship captains and crews crossing Hormuz earn so much they're 'almost being viewed as mercenaries'
articles.content_orig:
The high-risk, high-reward business of moving oil through the Strait of Hormuz has gotten riskier and more rewarding.
Despite steady attacks from Iran, oil tankers and other commercial vessels have continued flowing through the narrow waterway. With protection from the U.S. military and help from pipelines bypassing the strait, Persian Gulf oil flows returned to prewar levels .
But seeking to reassert its leverage over the global oil chokepoint, Iran has stepped up drone and missile strikes on ships recently, including those outside the immediate vicinity of Hormuz.
While traffic has dipped in response, ships continue to cross, with many making shuttle runs in and out of the Gulf to unload oil cargoes via ship-to-ship transfers. Then other vessels deliver the barrels to customers.
For those onboard the ships willing to tolerate the risks in the Gulf, a hefty payday awaits. Tanker captains can earn $100,000 a month for transiting the strait, plus a $50,000 bonus for each trip, sources told the Financial Times .
That “danger money” is up from regular pay of about $15,000 a month, and is necessary for shipowners to keep their fleets crewed.
Meanwhile, sailors typically make at little as $1,500 a month. But trips through Hormuz can bump up earnings by at least four to six times their normal rates, the report said.
Other hot spots also offer hazard enhancements, albeit less than what’s available for Hormuz trips. According to the FT , captains and sailors get double pay in the southern Red Sea , where Houthis have been attacking Saudi ships, and in the Gulf of Oman, where many ship-to-ship transfers take place after Hormuz shuttle runs.
Because many ships and their crews are dedicated to the shuttle runs, they are in constant peril—allowing them to stack up all the bonuses and danger money for each trip.
A source told the FT that those brave enough to stomach the near-constant threat of attacks are “almost being viewed as mercenaries,” though some unwilling crew members are reportedly being pressured to stay onboard.
Since the Iran war started on Feb. 28, at least 93 ships have been hit, and 24 sailors have been killed, according to the International Maritime Organization.
In addition to the hazard pay for crews, shipowners are also paying for insurance, and the war risk can command 6%-10% of a ship’s value—translating to up to $20 million for a supertanker sailing through the Gulf.
All the added costs have made shipping expensive too. Freight rates for cargoes crossing the Strait of Hormuz hit a record high of $1.3 million per day, up from last year’s daily rate of $20,000-$50,000.
All the ships needed to get oil out of the Gulf have also contributed to a global tanker shortage that’s spiked freight rates around the world.
Shipbroker Gibson pointed out that hiring a tanker to travel from the U.S. to China costs about $80 million, more than the $74 million price tag for a standard SpaceX Falcon 9 launch. Brokerage SSY estimated that rates are now the highest since the advent of the supertanker in the 1960s, even after adjusting for inflation.
Shipping costs have become so extreme that oil producers and even commodities traders are looking to own their own tankers to control the expenses.
But if freight costs get too high, they could erase the margins that can be earned from oil and refined fuels. For instance, European refiner Repsol saw its margin drop from $36 per barrel in the third quarter to $15 in October, according to analysts at RBC. Further reduction in margins could eventually force refiners to reduce how much crude they process.
The hazard premium could get worse in the Persian Gulf. Analysts have warned the Iranian regime, facing an existential threat to its rule, could re-escalate the war and take back its grip on the oil trade.
Esfandyar Batmanghelidj, founder and CEO of the Bourse & Bazaar Foundation think tank, pointed out recently that Iran can still destroy regional oil infrastructure, such as drilling and refining capacity, and can escalate if President Donald Trump rejects diplomatic off-ramps.
“Iran did not wage a scorched earth campaign—but it may yet do so if the current situation persists for too long,” he posted on X late last month. “That is what everyone who actually follows this region and its dynamics is worried about.”
Jason Ma is the weekend editor at Fortune , where he covers markets, the economy, finance, and housing.

articles.title_orig: Philadelphia police receive false homicide tip from Anthropic AI model
articles.title_zh: Philadelphia police receive false homicide tip from Anthropic AI model
articles.content_orig:
This report describes examples of unintended model actions we’ve observed during evaluations and internal use of Claude. It is part of our effort to publish more frequent standalone reports on model behavior and alignment beyond our system cards, which we publish with each model release, and our risk reports, which we publish every three to six months as part of our Responsible Scaling Policy. We believe it’s important to be transparent about what we see our models do during testing and use.
The behaviors can be grouped into four categories:
We have chosen not to name the organizations involved in the examples below to avoid exposing vulnerabilities in their systems, and at their request. For this reason, we also provide less detail about each case than we otherwise would. Some of the cases described below involved websites run by U.S. government agencies at the federal, state, and local levels. We have briefed the White House on these cases and notified each agency involved.
The cases we’ve identified to date in these categories had minimal real-world impact. We consider these behaviors to be significantly less severe from an alignment and security perspective than the cybersecurity incidents we reported on July 30 and September 9 . They resemble behaviors that we’ve described in our system cards since Claude Mythos Preview . Most are forms of persistence , in which Claude, when it cannot complete a task as given, works around a restriction instead of stopping.
Although the impact of these behaviors was minimal and we had already turned off live internet access for some high-risk and cybersecurity evaluations, we have now decided to expand that to include all our internal evaluations until we have confirmed that our security and monitoring measures (described in the remediation section of this post) reliably catch behaviors like these. Below, we also discuss alignment considerations and give more detail on how we’re modifying training to reduce the likelihood of further misbehavior.
We identified most of these cases through a review of transcripts that we began in July. Our review first focused on our cybersecurity evaluations—tests where a model is deliberately asked to probe or attack a test system, and where internet access is meant to be disabled. We have since extended our scanning to encompass a much wider range of instances where Claude could have reached the internet, including tests where internet access is deliberately enabled so Claude can be evaluated on real-world tasks. We began by looking for incidents of similar severity to the cybersecurity incidents we reported this summer; we have not found any to date. We then broadened the search to lower-severity cases, where a model interacted with real websites or systems in ways we didn’t intend.
We are also now scanning a much larger pool of lower-risk transcripts, as well as our use of Claude within Anthropic and in reinforcement learning (RL) environments where Claude has access to the internet. As this work continues, we plan to report new instances of unintended behaviors. All cases reported here involved Claude interacting with the outside world; to our knowledge, none of them involved customer data or Anthropic’s own internal systems.
In this post, we explain why we run evaluations, which are where most of these cases occurred; describe each behavior in more detail; and offer a preliminary view of what the behaviors suggest about Claude’s alignment and how we’re mitigating them.
The behaviors described in this post are not specific to evaluations, but many of the cases we’ve identified to date occurred during evaluation runs. We continually test models on a wide range of tasks prior to releasing them. We use many different evaluations (standardized sets of tasks, scored the same way each time), each of which helps to paint a picture of Claude’s skills in a particular area. Many of the evaluations we use are public; they are written by outside researchers and can be run by any developer, allowing us to compare capabilities across models. Other evaluations we build in-house.
Because language models are non-deterministic—that is, their responses always involve some element of randomness, and they may carry out the same task slightly differently each time—we have Claude complete each evaluation task hundreds or thousands of times (each attempt is called a run). Testing so many times allows us to understand how a model typically performs, and also to catch rare cases where a model does something we don’t expect. What we learn from evaluations shapes decisions across Anthropic, including how we train models, what safeguards we build around them, and when we release them.
Evaluations are also where a model’s behavioral issues are sometimes first revealed. Models learn much of what they can do through RL, in which they attempt a task within a specific environment many times over and are rewarded when they succeed. However, training environments are imperfect. If training rewards something we didn’t intend—such as finding loopholes or working around a restriction—the model learns that the workaround pays off and may then apply it elsewhere. This is known as reward hacking. While we have processes in place to identify and filter out reward hacking during training, evaluations are a critical mechanism for understanding a model’s behavioral propensities in different contexts and on different sets of tasks than those we have in training.
Some tasks—such as searching the web for hard-to-find information—are difficult to realistically simulate in an environment without internet access. Running them with access has been standard practice within the industry: public web search benchmarks are run on the live internet by default, and running them the same way allows us to compare our models with other models. Most of the cases in this report occurred during such evaluations.
Below, we describe four categories of behavior in which Claude acted on real websites and systems in ways we did not intend, each of which involved an organization or person outside Anthropic.
When Claude could not complete an evaluation task directly, either because its own tools were deliberately limited or because an outside service it needed was unavailable, it used other tools hosted on a third party’s site to achieve its goal. In some circumstances, it did this by exploiting basic flaws in that site’s software, using SQL or command injection (a way of sending input that the site mistakenly runs as instructions).
For example, one evaluation asked Claude Mythos Preview to run a scientific analysis. The public tool it needed to perform that analysis was hosted by a university; when the model sought to access it, the tool returned an error. Looking for another way to complete the task, Claude explored the tool’s website, found a script on the university’s server that would return any file it was asked for, and used it to copy files from the server, including the script’s own code. In that code Claude found the injection flaw that let it run commands on the server, and used it to run the calculation.
In another instance, the data Claude Mythos 5 needed was free, but Claude could not access it without accepting a data use agreement, which it did not have the tools to do. Claude used applications hosted on the website to load the page and accept the agreement on its behalf.
We saw this behavior on DeepSearchQA and BrowseComp (both public web research evaluations), on LABBench2 (a public biology research benchmark), and during internal evaluations.
We saw instances where Claude submitted an online form when it shouldn’t have. Generally, this occurred when an evaluation’s instructions were ambiguous, or when a misconfiguration within the environment prevented Claude from working with dummy forms.

articles.title_orig: Lee Claims World Gold as Tasoev Secures His Third World Title in Baku
articles.title_zh: Lee Claims World Gold as Tasoev Secures His Third World Title in Baku
articles.content_orig:
Today closes out the individual competition at the Baku World Judo Championships and it's time for the heavyweights to take centre stage in Azerbaijan.
Before the finals, the traditional flag-passing ceremony was held to commemorate the closing of the event, as Azerbaijan passed the IJF flag to Kazakhstan - with Astana set to host the World Championships in 2027.
At +78kg , 19 year old Hyeonji LEE was on fire enroute to the final, with ippon in every contest. With a World bronze from last year, she would be feeling confident that this was her moment to claim the red backpatch.
Facing her was Romane DICKO, a former World Champion and no stranger to the podium. DICKO would be looking to regain the mantle and become a two time World Champion. Displaying a groundwork masterclass today, could she repeat her former success?
In the final, LEE continued her dominant run and bested DICKO with a waza-ari that transitioned into a hold down. The Korean had written her name into history. A composed finish to a remarkable day that sealed the biggest title of her career.
IOC Member Ms Yael ARAD awarded the medals.
In the +100kg category, reigning double World Champion Inal TASOEV had come to Baku to earn his third title and looked in complete control on his route through the draw. Powerful and assured throughout the day, he arrived in the final with another World gold firmly within reach.
His opponent was Azerbaijan’s own Ushangi KOKAURI. With the crowd behind him, he had the chance to turn their energy into the biggest victory of his career. Every roar from the stands added pressure, but also belief that a home World title was possible.
In the +100kg final, TASOEV delivered a moment of pure judo feeling to score ippon, and achieve an incredible third World title. TASOEV will wear the red backpatch for another year. A commanding finish underlined his status as the man to beat.
Azerbaijan Minister of Youth and Sport Mr Farid GAYIBOV awarded the medals.
Join us tomorrow in Baku where the Mixed Team competition kicks off.

articles.title_orig: US man shoots off-duty ICE agent who allegedly attacked him and daughter
articles.title_zh: US man shoots off-duty ICE agent who allegedly attacked him and daughter
articles.content_orig:
ICE official, who was sleeping on man’s lawn and appeared ‘intoxicated’, faces felony charges, California police say
A 72-year-old man shot an off-duty Immigration and Customs Enforcement ( ICE ) official in California early on Friday morning after the “intoxicated and agitated” official assaulted him and his daughter on their property, local authorities allege.
The Fresno police department said that the ICE official was receiving medical care after being shot in the midsection. The official, identified as David Gonzalez, is facing felony charges for assaulting the father-daughter duo, Fresno police said .
It was not immediately clear for how long Gonzalez had been with ICE and what exactly he did for ICE. The Department of Homeland Security (DHS), which oversees ICE, referred all questions about Gonzalez to Fresno police.
According to Fresno police, at about 3am, a woman found Gonzalez sleeping on her and her father’s front lawn. She told her 72-year-old father, who was inside, and then attempted to shoo Gonzalez off their property.
But when Gonzalez was awakened, “he appeared intoxicated and agitated” and physically assaulted the 72-year-old father, forcing him to the ground, police said. When the father’s daughter tried to intervene, Gonzalez physically attacked and took her to the ground as well, police said.
The father feared for his and his daughter’s physical safety and shot Gonzalez once, police said. Shortly thereafter, the daughter’s boyfriend, an off-duty police officer, arrived and placed handcuffs on Gonzalez.
“It is unknown at this time why Gonzalez was in the area at the time of the [shooting], but it has been confirmed he was off-duty and alone,” local authorities said.
Fresno police on Friday said the investigation into the shooting was continuing while Gonzalez was in custody and receiving medical treatment. He was booked with battery likely to cause great bodily injury, felony vandalism and battery.
The father and daughter were not booked with any crimes as they recovered from injuries of their own, police said.
The confrontation that led to Gonzalez’s shooting is one of the latest cases in which federal ICE officials have fallen under scrutiny for alleged criminal behavior. ICE has also been met with nationwide criticism throughout Donald Trump ’s second term for the agency’s aggressive arrest, detention and deportation tactics.
after newsletter promotion
Lawmakers have also criticized ICE’s hiring practices amid the agency’s rush to bring on more officials to carry out the Trump administration’s mass deportation agenda. In August 2025, an ICE supervisor filed a whistleblower complaint to the DHS office of inspector general alleging that the agency was skirting basic vetting and violating federal rules during its hiring spree.
In July, an ICE officer shot and killed a Colombian immigrant in Biddeford, Maine. The ICE officer in question had reportedly been a recent hire by the agency despite an alleged history of violence and mental health problems.
Meanwhile, in April, a longtime ICE officer in Cincinnati was arrested after allegedly lying to DHS about domestic violence allegations against him. Local news reports say police had been called more than 20 times in the past to years to the home he shared with his girlfriend.
The Ohio Immigrant Alliance, a pro-immigrant group, released a report in August documenting more than 150 federal immigration officials accused of abuse and crimes. One of the latest entries in their report cited allegations that an ICE official reportedly broke into an ex-girlfriend’s apartment in south-east Louisiana.

articles.title_orig: Navarre, Gulf Breeze residents assess storm damage from Hurricane Isaias
articles.title_zh: Navarre, Gulf Breeze residents assess storm damage from Hurricane Isaias
articles.content_orig:
NAVARRE, Fla. ( WALA ) - Residents across the Navarre and Gulf Breeze area spent the day after the storm assessing damage, clearing debris and checking on neighbors.
Navarre Beach survives with minimal damage
As darkness still hung over the Florida Panhandle Saturday morning, Navarre Beach was a virtual ghost town. Residents had evacuated, left with the question of what they would find when they returned.
With daylight, it became clear the area was spared the worst of the storm. Homes were missing siding and had other superficial damage but appeared structurally sound.
Navarre Beach Fire Rescue Fire Chief, Jonathan Kanzigg was out early surveying damage.
“I am ecstatic about how the island looks right now. I had anticipated not being able to move a fire truck on the island which would inhibit our response, but the roads are good. I haven’t seen any structural damage to houses. A lot of superficial...roofs, siding, garage doors. Some houses won’t be inhabitable, but structurally everything looks amazing,” Kanzigg said.
Gulf Breeze, Milton see more severe damage
Damage was more severe to the west. On Highway 98 near Gulf Breeze, campers at Camping World were overturned by strong north winds from the back side of the storm’s eye wall, with one coming close to the highway. Convoys of tree trimming and debris removal crews mobilized in the area. Officials said the area took a significant hit from the western eye wall, with strong north winds downing fences and trees.
Bergren Road was covered in fallen pine trees. Leslie Holcombe spent the morning cutting out trees there and near her home in Milton, where she said the damage looked different.
“We can definitely see what look like tornado tracks up in Milton over and over. Lots of trees down, roofs gone,” Holcombe said.
Neighbors help clear roads
Mark Bergman was cutting a tree out of the roadway so he could check on his home.
“Multiple trees down along Bergren, so I had a chainsaw in my car in preparation for this just in case, to cut my way back, so we’ve been cutting our way through here on Bergren Road and then, a couple of folks from Milton have been here as well, helping cut the trees down and now we’ve got the Santa Rosa County Sheriff here about to pull this tree out of the way with a winch,” Bergman said.
Asked whether people were coming together, Bergman said, “Yeah, they’re coming together. Everyone’s pitching in, taking care of each other which is what it’s all about.”
State crews assist with cleanup
State crews with the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission arrived to help finish clearing trees and reopen the neighborhood.
Public and government agencies worked together through the day to begin restoring the area on the way to recovery.

articles.title_orig: Microsoft offers MacBook Pro owners up to $1,000 to switch to Surface Laptop Ultra
articles.title_zh: Microsoft offers MacBook Pro owners up to $1,000 to switch to Surface Laptop Ultra
articles.content_orig:
Microsoft is ready to pay MacBook owners to switch to its new Surface Laptop Ultra. The company is offering MacBook Pro owners up to $1,000 in promotional cash back on top of their trade-in value when they preorder the new laptop.
The cash back is paid on top of the standard trade-in value rather than being deducted from the purchase price at checkout. To receive cash back, buyers must purchase a qualifying Surface Laptop Ultra and submit an online trade-in claim with proof of purchase. After Microsoft’s trade-in partner receives and evaluates the MacBook, the customer receives its trade-in value plus any promotional cash back they qualify for.
The deal runs through November 23 in the US and Canada. The MacBook must meet Microsoft’s condition requirements and be mailed within 15 days of completing the trade-in process. The promotional bonus varies based on the device and its trade-in value, up to the advertised $1,000 maximum.
The Surface Laptop Ultra starts at $2,599.99, making it the least expensive laptop in the RTX Spark lineup. Microsoft is positioning the machine as a high-performance option for power users, with Nvidia’s RTX Spark platform featuring an 18-core or 20-core CPU, an RTX GPU with up to 6,144 CUDA cores, and 24GB to 128GB of unified memory. Other highlights include a mini-LED display and a wide selection of ports, including a proprietary magnetic USB-C port.
The trade-in value itself varies depending on the MacBook Pro model and its condition. The source reports that the highest estimate it obtained from Microsoft’s website was $2,115 for a 16-inch MacBook Pro from 2025 equipped with 128GB of RAM and a 4TB SSD. Adding the maximum $1,000 promotional bonus could bring the total value to $3,115, although the final amount depends on the device and its eligibility for the offer.
The offer is a clear attempt to attract customers from Apple's premium laptop lineup. Rather than competing only on hardware and performance, Microsoft is giving MacBook Pro owners a financial incentive to switch platforms.
Preorders for the Surface Laptop Ultra are available through Microsoft’s website and Best Buy, with shipments set to begin on October 16.

Break out the birthday balloons for the bull market .
Investors are currently living in the 11th bull market since the 1950s, which is on track to become the seventh to complete at least four full years on Oct. 12, according to a new analysis by Truist co-chief investment officer Keith Lerner.
Measured against every bull market dating back to the 1950s, the 119% advance sits near the middle of the pack, well below the 401% gain during the 2009-2020 cycle and the 582% gain from 1987-2000.
Read more: What is a bull market?
The historical average advance for a bull market in Lerner's measurement period is 184%. Of the 10 prior bull markets, six lasted longer than four years.
Among bull markets that reached this stage, the fifth year produced an average return of 12% and a median return of 15%.
"The weight of the evidence remains supportive as the bull market enters its fifth year," Lerner wrote. "Continued economic growth, resilient corporate profits, and a meaningful reset in valuations provide a solid foundation for maintaining a constructive stance. At the same time, history suggests investors should not get caught off guard by volatility as the cycle matures."
The bull market this year has been powered by the one-two punch of strong corporate earnings and AI optimism.
The S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) is expected to report year-over-year earnings growth of 29.5% for the recently completed third quarter.
If that plays out, it will mark the third consecutive quarter of earnings growth above 25%, according to FactSet. It would also represent the eighth straight quarter of double-digit percentage earnings growth.
For the fourth quarter, Wall Street analysts are calling for earnings growth of 27.6%. And for all of 2026, analysts are predicting year-over-year earnings growth of 32.4%.
Earnings estimates for 2027 are already on the rise, especially for tech names amid unrelenting AI demand.
About 40% of the year-to-date revisions to S&P 500 earnings estimates for 2026 are attributable to the semiconductor and hardware industries, according to a new analysis from Barclays strategist Venu Krishna.

The SEC showdown between Georgia and Alabama could experience some weather effects, but not as drastic as some feared when Hurricane Isaias was racing toward the Gulf Coast.
The AccuWeather forecast for the 7:30 p.m. kickoff (TV: ABC) between the teams at Bryant-Denny Stadium in Tuscaloosa, Alabama, calls for temperatures in the mid-60s with cloudy skies and a 20-25 percent chance of rain and winds between 7 to 16 miles per hour.
That said, there’s a possibility wind gusts could affect the passing game plans of Georgia and Alabama, which rank No. 1 and No. 2 in the nation in scoring, the Bulldogs at 51.4 points per game, the Tide averaging 49.6 points per game.
Georgia’s Gunner Stockton ranks third in the nation with 75.5% completion rate, while Alabama’s Keelon Russell is 14th in the country, completing 71.2% of his passes.
Isaias has dissipated to a post-tropical cyclone since making landfall as a Category 2 hurricane over Destin, Florida, at 9:30 p.m. on Friday with sustained wind speeds of more than 105 mph.
Radar indicates the front has moved out of Alabama, leaving behind a remnant of rain.
Tuscaloosa County, which was among the 40 counties in Alabama include in a state of emergency declared on Wednesday as authorities prepared for the worst, remains under a wind advisory that’s in effect until 8 p.m (eastern) on Saturday.
The rainfall isn’t expected to have much, if any, effect on the game as Bryant-Denny Stadium installed a vacuum-assisted drainage system in 2023.
The SubAir system is notably the same as the one at Augusta National Golf Club.
The threat of inclement weather led many, including President Donald Trump, to cancel their plans to attend the game.
The tickets for sale on the secondary market are much lower than expected. The lowest-priced tickets on Ticketmaster could be had for $133.34 each.

articles.title_orig: Galaxy Z Fold 8 is already beating the foldable iPhone in a way I can’t ignore
articles.title_zh: Galaxy Z Fold 8 is already beating the foldable iPhone in a way I can’t ignore
articles.content_orig:
Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.
When I first got my hands on the iPhone Duo , I admittedly dismissed the unfolding animation that would soon become a highlight of online discourse. I was less interested in the smooth transition as content shifted from one screen to another and more focused on details such as the matte inner display and seemingly invisible crease.
But in the weeks since Apple unveiled its first foldable iPhone, which drops Oct. 23 , I’ve seen countless examples on social media of people trying to recreate that buzzed-about animation on their Android foldables. While the Play Store offers plenty of launchers for customizing Android phones — including ones that mimic the iPhone’s home screen — this appears to be one iOS design element that users are particularly eager to bring to their devices.
Sometimes, you really can’t predict what people will care about most — or the lengths they’ll go to imitate a feature.
The primary phone people have used to recreate the iPhone Duo’s cascading transition effect is Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 , which debuted in July with a passport-size foldable design ahead of Apple’s release . Unlike iOS, Samsung’s One UI interface, which runs on top of Android on Galaxy devices, doesn’t include a folding animation. Instead, content simply transitions from the Z Fold 8’s cover screen to its inner display once the phone is opened about halfway. I never considered this a deficiency until I saw the flood of positive reactions to the iPhone Duo’s fluid transition effect.
To bridge that gap, several creators have posted videos explaining how to use third-party apps and developer tools on GitHub to get a similar effect on the Z Fold 8, with caveats like “ the smoothness and quality won’t be the same ‘” and “ install it [at] your own risk .” (That’s encouraging!) The steps don’t seem particularly complicated, and some options appear to have cropped up in the Play Store as well.
I’ve chosen to forgo installing these Duo-copycat apps on my precious Galaxy Z Fold 8 for two reasons. First, I’m not much of a risk-taker. Second, I’m not interested in imitating an aesthetic element of Apple’s software with a derivative version, especially when the Galaxy Z Fold 8 is a standout foldable device in its own right. While the value of the Duo’s sleek animation has since grown on me, I’m not quite desperate enough to retrofit it onto a foldable phone that’s just as functional without that flourish.
Don’t get me wrong: I think Apple’s combination of hardware and software expertise will elevate the iPhone Duo in a way that merits the attention the phone has received, despite being relatively “late” to the foldables game . But I also think it’s more tasteful for consumers to embrace what each phone-maker does best, rather than shoehorning in a competitor’s feature for something as superficial as an animation effect.
The Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 is one of my favorite phones I’ve tested this year, earning it a CNET Editors’ Choice Award. Its versatile design is optimized for both vertical and horizontal content : I can stream YouTube videos and movies on the 7.6-inch inner display, then rotate it to seamlessly scroll through social posts. The crease is barely noticeable, and the battery easily lasts all day. The 5.5-inch cover screen never feels cramped, while its sharp corners give the phone a highly polished look. And despite lacking a telephoto lens, the Z Fold 8’s dual rear cameras pull their weight, capturing crisp, vibrant photos.
The iPhone Duo shares many attributes with the Z Fold 8, including a palm-size design, 7.6-inch inner display and dual rear cameras. Those similarities prompted Samsung to post a series of salty tweets after Apple debuted its foldable last month, including one that reads , “Let us know when you’re done reheating our leftovers.”
That said, I am curious how app developers might optimize their platforms for the iPhone Duo in ways we haven’t seen with other foldable phones. While the Android operating system spans a wide range of devices and configurations, iOS developers only have to cater to a single foldable, potentially leading to a more tailored and streamlined experience. We got a glimpse of how Netflix is building its app for the Duo, and it’ll be interesting to see how both Apple and other third-party developers take full advantage of the phone’s 1.4:1 aspect ratio in ways that could make its predecessors seem behind the curve in that regard.
“Borrowing” features from each other is what phone-makers do best. Down the road, it’s possible companies such as Samsung will implement foldable capabilities that Apple rolled out first, and vice versa. Heck, Apple’s delayed entry into this space means it had time to analyze what worked well for its competitors before jumping in with its own rendition. It’s just how the industry works.
So maybe the Galaxy Z Fold 9 — or whatever Samsung decides to call the follow-up to the Z Fold 8 — will have its own nifty opening animation. But until Samsung itself embraces the idea, I’ll stick with using the standout foldable as-is.

articles.title_zh: Exclusive | At Davos, Kimberly Guilfoyle Boasted of Private Jet Trips, Luxury Stays
articles.content_orig:
Eric Deters says US ambassador to Greece asked him to pay off American Express credit card bill in return for access
A Trump donor accused Kimberly Guilfoyle, the US ambassador to Greece and Trump family ally, of engaging in a “quid pro quo” by asking him to pay off her $100,000 debt in exchange for access to administration officials.
Eric Deters, a former congressional candidate and lawyer, told MS Now on Thursday that Guilfoyle had “ambushed” him last year with an offer to provide access to government officials if he paid her American Express credit card bill, before her US Senate confirmation hearing as ambassador to Greece.
“It absolutely was a quid pro quo,” Deters told the network in response to a Wall Street Journal report that she had pushed him for the money.
“Kimberly Guilfoyle is a grifter,” he added.
The Guardian has asked Guilfoyle’s lawyer for comment.
Jesse Binnall, a lawyer for Guilfoyle, told the Wall Street Journal that Guilfoyle disputed the authenticity of the messages, but that she was “owed a balance” for travel and speaking at events before her nomination. Deters told the Journal that he did not owe Guilfoyle any balance.
The report is the latest allegation about Guilfoyle’s conduct as a US official. Deters shared messages he and Guilfoyle exchanged in which the US ambassador to Greece promised him “ride or die” access to Trump administration officials if he wired American Express $100,000.
Asked about the report during a press conference in Athens on Wednesday, Marco Rubio , the US secretary of state, said he would not address the allegations. He reaffirmed his support for the US embassy in Greece adding, “ Our ambassador has been a strong ambassador here.” Asked again about the reports on Thursday, Rubio refused to comment.
The top Democrats on the House foreign affairs and Senate foreign relations committees have asked Rubio to open an investigation into Guilfoyle’s conduct as an ambassador.
A spokesperson for the Democratic staff of the Senate foreign relations committee confirmed to the Guardian that they were requesting further information and continuing to investigate.
JD Vance similarly expressed hesitation, similar to Rubio, on Thursday when asked to respond to a US ambassador offering access to government officials in exchange for money to pay off debts.
“With that hypothetical, Jen, obviously I don’t love that,” the vice-president replied. “But I don’t know exactly who you’re talking about. I don’t know the full details. What I find with these stories is you never want to comment in a purely abstract way because a lot of times the details really matter,” he added.
Concerns about Guilfoyle’s conduct were first raised in September when the Wall Street Journal reported she had used her position to invite Greek lobbyists to sit in on official diplomatic meetings and promoted the business interests of one particular Greek construction and energy company.
Senator Jeanne Shaheen, the ranking Democrat on the Senate foreign relations committee, sent a letter to Rubio on Tuesday , asking him to look into the allegations against Guilfoyle.
“Such actions do not serve US credibility overseas and risk undermining US diplomacy,” Shaheen wrote. “In advance of your upcoming travel to Greece , I request an immediate review of Ambassador Guilfoyle’s actions and a clarification of what steps have and will be taken to avoid undue influence and even the appearance of a conflict of interest.”
Separately, Gregory Meeks, the ranking Democrat on the House foreign affairs committee, sent a letter to Rubio in September, requesting more information about Guilfoyle’s conduct, her relationship with the Greek construction and energy company and her relationship with the lobbyist.
“If these reports are accurate, Ambassador Guilfoyle is unfit to represent the United States abroad and should be removed from her position,” Meeks wrote.
Guilfoyle, 57, was once a member of the Trump family’s inner circle, having been engaged to Donald Trump Jr, the US president’s eldest son, for roughly three years. The couple ended their engagement in 2024, and shortly after taking office, Donald Trump nominated Guilfoyle to be ambassador to Greece.
But now further allegations accuse Guilfoyle of promising a Trump donor, Eric Deters, access to the Trump administration in exchange for a $100,000 payment to American Express.
Deters shared messages exchanged between himself and Guilfoyle with the Wall Street Journal in which she reportedly pleaded: “Honey please I need you to get this done for me today.”
Deters said Guilfoyle had promised him thatshe would “be your Trump ride or die, forever and ever” if he made the American Express balance. Deters said he never made the payment.
In other messages, Guilfoyle reportedly raised concerns about her communications with Deters becoming public and reprimanded him for not being discreet. “Eric, I really wish you would stop papering all these things. It’s really dangerous and not helpful to you or me while you could simply just call me on Signal,” she is said to have written in one message.
“What a nightmare, you’ll literally cost me my ambassadorship stop writing,” Guilfoyle reportedly wrote in another message.
A lawyer for Guilfoyle disputed the authenticity of messages Deters shared with the Wall Street Journal.
It is unclear whether Shaheen or Meeks will ask Rubio for further information about the latest report. The Guardian has asked Meeks and Shaheen for comment.
